en.editorNote: Tag the friend who caught themselves starting to save 'good morning' graphics
variations: Easy way to tell you've grown up: you used to laugh at the good-morning graphics, now you collect them.
Junior adult leaves the family chat on read. Senior adult is the one reminding everyone to bundle up, drink water, and stay home during the typhoon.

items.sourceNote: 初級大人/高級大人 contrast; original angle on splitting the restaurant bill (not previously covered)

zh-tw.content:
初級大人分帳：帳單來了，全桌突然安靜，低頭滑手機假裝在算，其實在等別人先開口喬。

高級大人分帳：打開分帳 App，「一人 380，我先付，等等轉給我。」三十秒解決。

差別不是誰比較有錢，是誰願意當那個先開口的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次聚餐帳單一來就突然安靜、盯著桌面的朋友
variations: 初級大人算 AA：掏出計算機，還要問「你剛剛那杯飲料要不要另外算？」高級大人算 AA：直接平分，多的幾十塊誰在意。
帳單放到桌上的那一刻，才看得出一桌人誰是高級大人。

en.content:
Junior adult splitting the bill: the check arrives, the whole table goes quiet and stares at their phones pretending to do math, secretly waiting for someone else to sort it out.

Senior adult splitting the bill: opens the split app — 'It's $28 each, I'll cover it, just send it over.' Done in thirty seconds.

The difference isn't who has more money. It's who's willing to be the one who speaks up first.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend who goes dead silent and stares at the table the second the check lands
variations: Junior adult splitting evenly: pulls out the calculator and asks 'wait, do we count the drink you had separately?' Senior adult: just splits it down the middle, who cares about the extra few bucks.
The moment the check hits the table is when you find out who at it is a real grown-up.

items.sourceNote: 初級大人/高級大人 social maturity angle; original take on gracefully accepting a compliment

zh-tw.content:
初級大人被稱讚：「這件很好看耶！」「沒有啦，很便宜，隨便穿的。」耳朵紅到脖子，急著把功勞推掉。

高級大人被稱讚：「這件很好看耶！」「對吧，我挑很久，謝謝你發現。」

學會好好收下一句稱讚，比學會賺錢還難。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被誇獎第一反應永遠是「沒有啦」、然後渾身不自在的朋友
variations: 初級大人收到讚美：先否認三次。高級大人收到讚美：微笑說謝謝，然後真心開心一整天。
長大的其中一課，是學會不再急著把每句好話推回去。

en.content:
Junior adult getting a compliment: 'That looks great on you!' 'Oh, this? It was cheap, I just threw it on.' Ears turning red, rushing to give the credit away.

Senior adult getting a compliment: 'That looks great on you!' 'Right? Took me forever to pick, thanks for noticing.'

Learning to actually accept a compliment is harder than learning to make money.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend whose first reaction to any praise is 'oh, it's nothing' followed by full-body awkwardness
variations: Junior adult receiving praise: denies it three times first. Senior adult: smiles, says thank you, and is quietly thrilled about it all day.
One of the quieter lessons of growing up is learning to stop shoving every kind word back.

items.sourceNote: 以為長大後 format; original angle on housework being an endless loop

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為長大後有了自己的家，就能永遠住在整齊漂亮的空間裡。

長大後才發現，家事是一種沒有終點的循環：碗洗好，只是在等下一餐變髒；地拖乾淨，灰塵已經在排隊了。

所謂維持一個家，就是把同一件事，做一輩子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛收好家裡、轉頭又亂掉、默默嘆氣的同住戰友
variations: 初級大人：以為大掃除一次就能一勞永逸。高級大人：知道整潔不是狀態，是每天的維護。
沒有人告訴你，長大後有一半的時間，都在把東西弄乾淨，然後看著它再髒一次。

en.content:
As a kid I thought that once I grew up and had my own place, I'd get to live in a clean, beautiful space forever.

Turns out housework is a loop with no finish line: the dishes are clean, just waiting for the next meal to dirty them; the floor's mopped, and the dust is already lining up.

Keeping a home just means doing the same tasks over and over, for the rest of your life.
en.editorNote: Tag the roommate who just tidied the whole place, turned around, and sighed as it fell apart again
variations: Junior adult: thinks one big deep-clean will fix it for good. Senior adult: knows tidiness isn't a state, it's daily maintenance.
Nobody warns you that half of adulthood is cleaning things and then watching them get dirty all over again.

items.sourceNote: 2026 保健食品趨勢；改寫成初級/高級大人對照原創

zh-tw.content:
初級大人吃保健食品：買了一罐維他命，吃三天就忘在抽屜裡，過期了才想起來。

高級大人吃保健食品：一個七格藥盒，葉黃素、魚油、B群分好，早餐後準時服用，比吃正餐還規律。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個桌上開始擺一排罐子的朋友，恭喜正式進入養生階段
variations: 初級大人：保健食品是媽媽硬塞的。高級大人：保健食品是自己主動加購，還會比成分。

en.content:
Junior adult and supplements: buys one bottle of vitamins, takes them for three days, forgets them in a drawer, finds them again after they expire.

Senior adult and supplements: a seven-day pill organizer with omega-3, lutein, and B-complex all sorted, taken right after breakfast, more punctual than actual meals.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend whose kitchen counter is slowly turning into a pharmacy shelf
variations: Junior adult: takes supplements only because mom shoved them in your bag. Senior adult: buys them yourself and compares the ingredient labels.

items.sourceNote: 自備環保杯/購物袋主題；改寫成對照原創

zh-tw.content:
初級大人買手搖：站在店門口才想到環保杯又忘在家，默默多付了兩塊。

高級大人買手搖：環保杯放包包、放車上、放辦公室各一個，購物袋摺成小方塊塞在每一個口袋，走到哪都不怕。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個包包裡永遠掏得出一個購物袋的朋友
variations: 初級大人：結帳才發現沒帶袋子，抱著一堆東西走出超市。高級大人：袋子早就在手上攤開了。

en.content:
Junior adult buying bubble tea: remembers the reusable cup is at home the moment they reach the counter, quietly pays the extra fee.

Senior adult buying bubble tea: a reusable cup in the bag, one in the car, one at the office, and a tote folded into a neat little square in every pocket. Always ready.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend who can pull a folded tote bag out of thin air at checkout
variations: Junior adult: realizes at the register there's no bag, walks out of the store hugging groceries. Senior adult: already had the tote open before the beep.

items.sourceNote: 囤塑膠袋/紙袋主題；改寫成獨立語錄原創

zh-tw.content:
每個大人的家裡，都有一個裝滿塑膠袋的塑膠袋。

你從來不記得自己去買過袋子，它們卻越積越多，好像在裡面自己繁殖。

你捨不得丟，因為「總有一天會用到」——然後那一天，你會再去買一個新的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個抽屜或門後掛著一大包袋子的室友，你們是同一種人
variations: 紙箱也是。網購來的箱子疊在陽台，理由是「搬家可以用」，結果搬家那天全部一起丟。
衣櫃深處那疊摺得整整齊齊的紙袋，你永遠留著，也永遠沒在用。

en.content:
Every adult's home has one plastic bag stuffed full of other plastic bags.

You never remember buying a single one, yet they keep multiplying, like they're breeding in there.

You can't throw them out, because "they'll come in handy someday" — and on that someday, you'll go buy a brand-new one.
en.editorNote: Tag the roommate with a bulging bag-of-bags behind the pantry door — you two are the same species
variations: Same goes for cardboard boxes. They pile up on the balcony because "they're good for moving," then get tossed all at once on moving day.
That neat stack of paper gift bags in the back of the closet: kept forever, used never.

items.sourceNote: 手搖飲糖度演變主題；改寫成小時候/長大後語錄原創

zh-tw.content:
小時候點手搖，理所當然是全糖加珍珠，甜到喉嚨黏住才夠味。

長大後站在櫃檯前，聽見自己說出：「微糖去冰，珍珠換寒天。」

然後心裡默默補一句：其實無糖也可以。你不是變養生，你是被身體警告過了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個糖度一路從全糖降到無糖的朋友，一起哀悼回不去的味蕾
variations: 從全糖到七分到微糖到無糖，這條路上，你失去的不是甜，是青春。
你知道你長大了，不是因為會存錢，是因為你開始覺得全糖「太甜了喝不下」。

en.content:
As a kid, ordering bubble tea meant full sugar with extra pearls, sweet enough to glue your throat shut. That was the whole point.

As an adult, you hear yourself say at the counter: "Quarter sugar, less ice, swap the pearls for something lighter."

Then you think, quietly: honestly, zero sugar would be fine too. You didn't get healthier. Your body just filed a complaint.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend whose sugar level has slid all the way from full to zero — mourn your lost taste buds together
variations: Full sugar, to half, to a quarter, to none. On that road, what you lost wasn't sweetness. It was your youth.
You know you're an adult not when you start saving money, but when full sugar starts tasting "way too sweet to finish."

items.sourceNote: 買鞋看好不好走主題；改寫成初級/高級大人對照原創

zh-tw.content:
初級大人買鞋：先看好不好看，穿起來磨腳、走一小時就痛，也忍著，反正拍照好看就好。

高級大人買鞋：進店第一句問「這雙好不好走？」試穿在店裡繞三圈，好看是加分，能走一整天不痛才是重點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個鞋櫃裡漂亮的鞋越來越少、好走的鞋越來越多的朋友
variations: 初級大人：為了穿搭忍痛穿高跟。高級大人：包包裡永遠備一雙折疊平底鞋。

en.content:
Junior adult buying shoes: looks at the style first. They pinch, they hurt after an hour, but who cares, they photograph well.

Senior adult buying shoes: first question in the store is "are these comfortable to walk in?" Loops around the shop three times to test. Good-looking is a bonus; walking all day pain-free is the whole point.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend whose shoe rack has fewer pretty pairs and more comfortable ones every year
variations: Junior adult: suffers through heels for the outfit. Senior adult: always keeps a pair of foldable flats in the bag.

items.sourceNote: summer-break-as-an-adult meme theme; rewritten into an original 小時候/長大後 quote about July

zh-tw.content:
小時候的七月，是兩個月暑假的開場：早上睡到自然醒，下午泡在游泳池，作業留到最後三天再一次補完。

長大後的七月，只是一個有三十一天的月份。想休假要先看行事曆、跟同事喬、跟主管報備，請完假回來還要補上那五天的進度。

最殘忍的是，天氣一模一樣熱。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看到學生放暑假就開始懷疑人生的同事
variations: 長大後最公平的一件事：暑假結束了，但夏天沒有。
小時候數著暑假還剩幾天，長大後數著特休還剩幾天。

en.content:
July as a kid was the opening act of a two-month break: sleeping until you woke up on your own, afternoons in the pool, saving every worksheet for the last three days.

July as an adult is just a month with thirty-one days in it. Time off means checking the calendar, trading days with coworkers, clearing it with your manager, and then catching up on a week of work the moment you're back.

The cruelest part is that the weather is exactly as hot as it always was.
en.editorNote: Tag the coworker who has a small existential crisis every time they see kids out of school
variations: The fairest thing about growing up: summer break ended, but summer didn't.
As a kid you counted the days left of summer break. Now you count the days left of your PTO.

items.sourceNote: 2026 夏季電價 6/1-9/30、夏月帳單平均多約 446 元；改寫成原創語錄，非對照格式

zh-tw.content:
夏季電價從六月一號開始，你其實一直都知道。

可是七月的中午三十六度，你還是會走過去把冷氣按下去，然後在心裡跟自己談判：只開一小時、設二十七度、待會就關。

帳單來的時候，多出來的那四百多塊躺在那裡，你看著它嘆一口氣，然後繼續開。

所謂成熟，就是知道代價，還是選擇讓自己活下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每年夏天都在冷氣跟電費之間天人交戰的室友
variations: 小時候熱了就開冷氣，長大後熱了要先算這個月已經用掉幾度。
夏天最貴的不是出去玩，是你只想好好睡一覺。

en.content:
Summer electricity rates kick in on June 1. You've known that the whole time.

And still, at noon in July when it's ninety-seven degrees, you walk over and turn the AC on, negotiating with yourself the entire way: just an hour, set it to eighty, I'll shut it off soon.

Then the bill arrives with an extra fifteen bucks sitting on it. You look at it, sigh, and turn the AC on again.

Maturity is knowing exactly what it costs and choosing to survive anyway.
en.editorNote: Tag the roommate who fights the same war between comfort and the power bill every single summer
variations: As a kid, hot meant turn on the AC. As an adult, hot means first checking how much you've already burned through this month.
The most expensive thing about summer isn't the trip. It's wanting one good night's sleep.

items.sourceNote: adulthood meme theme of adult obligations; original angle on wedding-season red envelopes (existing 紅包 items are all Lunar New Year)

zh-tw.content:
這幾年的週末開始長得很像：這個月兩場婚禮，下個月一場滿月酒，行事曆比大學社團時期還滿。

你笑著說恭喜，包了一個不失禮的數字，回家打開帳戶餘額，又笑了一次，這次笑得比較小聲。

沒有人教過你，替別人開心也是要付費的——而且你其實真心願意付。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個婚禮季一到就開始盤點紅包預算的朋友
variations: 二十五歲的週末在夜店，三十五歲的週末在婚宴會館，穿的都還是同一件襯衫。
紅包金額會隨著年紀自動往上加，這是一種沒有人公告過的通貨膨脹。

en.content:
After a certain age your weekends start to look the same: two weddings this month, a baby shower next month, a calendar fuller than it ever was in college.

You smile, say congratulations, and put a respectable number in the card. Then you get home, check your balance, and smile again — a lot more quietly this time.

Nobody warned you that being happy for other people costs money. Or that you'd genuinely be willing to pay it.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend who starts budgeting for wedding season the moment the first invite lands
variations: At twenty-five your weekends were at bars, at thirty-five they're at banquet halls, and it's the same one good shirt either way.
The number you write in the card goes up every year. It's inflation nobody ever officially announced.

items.sourceNote: adulting struggle memes; original angle on paying for phone storage instead of deleting photos

zh-tw.content:
手機跳出「儲存空間不足」，你點進去看：三萬七千張照片，一半是截圖，一半是同一隻貓的連拍。

你很認真地刪了十分鐘，刪掉四張，空出零點一 GB。

然後你按下「升級方案，每月九十元」。

大人處理問題的方式，常常不是解決它，是付錢請它先不要吵。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個相簿永遠 99% 滿、卻一張都捨不得刪的朋友
variations: 長大後你會有一堆小額月費，每一筆都是在買「暫時不用面對某件事」的權利。
刪照片跟整理衣櫃一樣：站在那裡很久，最後什麼都沒丟。

en.content:
Your phone flashes "Storage Almost Full." You open it up: thirty-seven thousand photos, half of them screenshots, half of them burst shots of the same cat.

You delete very seriously for ten minutes. You delete four pictures. You free up 0.1 GB.

Then you tap "Upgrade — $2.99 a month."

The adult way of handling a problem is usually not solving it, but paying it to stop bothering you.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend whose photo library is permanently 99% full and who can't bear to delete a single one
variations: Adulthood comes with a pile of small monthly fees, and every one of them buys the right to not deal with something yet.
Deleting photos is like cleaning out your closet: you stand there for ages and throw away nothing.

items.sourceNote: summer bug memes; rewritten into an original 3 a.m. mosquito quote about nobody coming to rescue you

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，耳邊那聲「嗡——」把你叫醒。

小時候你會喊媽，然後翻個身繼續睡，剩下的事有人處理。

現在你摸黑坐起來、開燈、拿電蚊拍，站在床上揮了十五分鐘，打到了，牆上留下一個紀念，回到床上再也睡不著。

早上七點鬧鐘照樣響，你照樣去上班。長大就是這樣：沒有人會來救你，但你救得了自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個昨晚跟蚊子單挑到三點半、今天靠咖啡續命的同事
variations: 大人的深夜三大敵人：蚊子、鄰居的裝潢，還有自己突然想起的黑歷史。
小時候被蚊子咬會哭，長大後被蚊子咬只是抹一下，然後繼續開會。

en.content:
Three in the morning, and that one high whine right next to your ear wakes you up.

As a kid you'd yell for your mom, roll over, and fall back asleep. Somebody else handled the rest.

Now you sit up in the dark, turn on the light, grab the swatter, and stand on your own bed swinging for fifteen minutes. You get it. There's a small memorial on the wall. You lie back down and never fall asleep again.

The alarm still goes off at seven. You still go to work. That's growing up: nobody's coming to save you, but you can save yourself.
en.editorNote: Tag the coworker who fought a mosquito until 3:30 a.m. and is running purely on coffee today
variations: The three great enemies of an adult night: mosquitoes, the neighbor's renovation, and a memory from ten years ago that shows up uninvited.
As a kid a mosquito bite made you cry. Now you rub it once and stay on the call.

items.sourceNote: 'Adulting is just Googling how to do things while hoping nobody notices' viral line; rewritten original

zh-tw.content: 小時候以為大人什麼都會，長大才發現，所謂大人就是一邊點頭說「這個交給我」，一邊躲進廁所偷偷 Google「這個到底要怎麼用」，然後祈禱沒人發現。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個開會時很鎮定、私訊裡瘋狂問你怎麼弄的同事
variations: 大人的自信，有一半是裝的，另一半是剛剛查到的。

en.content: As a kid you thought adults just knew things. Turns out being an adult is nodding 'yeah, I've got this' out loud while frantically Googling 'how does this actually work' in the bathroom and praying nobody notices.
en.editorNote: Tag the coworker who looks unshakeable in meetings and DMs you 'wait how do I do this' thirty seconds later
variations: Half of an adult's confidence is faked. The other half is something they looked up two minutes ago.

items.sourceNote: 'Money comes in quietly and leaves dramatically' / payday gone in 60 seconds; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
薪水入帳那一刻，你覺得自己是有錢人。

三十秒後，房租、卡費、保費、訂閱通通自動扣款，安安靜靜進來，轟轟烈烈離開，你又變回原本的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個月五號很闊氣、六號就開始吃泡麵的朋友
variations: 薪水像過境的觀光客：來拍個照，什麼都沒留下就走了。

en.content:
The second your paycheck lands, you feel rich.

Thirty seconds later rent, credit cards, insurance, and every subscription auto-deduct — money comes in quietly and leaves dramatically — and you're right back to being you.
en.editorNote: Tag the friend who's a baller on the 1st and eating instant noodles by the 3rd
variations: A paycheck is like a tourist passing through: shows up, takes a photo, leaves nothing behind.

items.sourceNote: 'Salary is the consolation prize for surviving adulthood'; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為薪水是努力工作的獎勵。

長大才懂，薪水其實是公司每個月頒給你的安慰獎，上面寫著：「恭喜你又撐過一個月，請繼續。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個月底看到入帳通知只想苦笑的社畜朋友
variations: 薪水不是獎金，是續命的儲值卡，剛好夠你撐到下一次入帳。

en.content:
As a kid you thought your salary was the reward for working hard.

Grown up, you get it: salary is the consolation prize they hand you every month, and it reads, 'Congrats on surviving another one. Please continue.'
en.editorNote: Tag the coworker whose only reaction to the deposit alert is a tired little laugh
variations: Salary isn't a bonus, it's a top-up card for your life — just enough to reach the next payday.

items.sourceNote: 'My dreams are expensive, and my budget disagrees'; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
我的夢想很貴，我的存款很有意見。

每次我一興奮打開購物車，銀行 App 就默默彈出餘額，像一個很冷靜的大人在旁邊說：「我們談談。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個把想要的東西放進購物車、放了半年還在放的朋友
variations: 理想生活跟實際預算，是分手很多次還一直復合的一對。

en.content:
My dreams are expensive and my savings have strong opinions.

Every time I excitedly open my cart, the banking app quietly shows me my balance, like a very calm adult going, 'We need to talk.'
en.editorNote: Tag the friend who's had the same item sitting in their cart for six months
variations: The life I want and the budget I have are a couple that keeps breaking up and getting back together.

items.sourceNote: 成年人成熟語錄 self-compassion theme; rewritten original with warmth

zh-tw.content:
到了某個年紀才慢慢明白，真正的成熟不是把自己逼得多緊，也不是什麼都扛得住。

是懂得在很累的那天，對自己說一句：「今天先到這裡吧，剩下的我明天再繼續。」然後真的放下，好好去睡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是把自己排在最後、該休息的時候還在硬撐的人
variations: 成熟不是不再累，是累的時候願意先照顧自己，而不是先罵自己。

en.content:
At some point you slowly realize real maturity isn't about how hard you push yourself, or carrying everything without cracking.

It's being able to tell yourself on a rough day, 'That's enough for now — the rest can wait till tomorrow,' and actually putting it down and getting some sleep.
en.editorNote: Send it to the person who always puts themselves last and keeps grinding when they should be resting
variations: Maturity isn't never being tired. It's choosing to take care of yourself when you are, instead of beating yourself up first.

items.sourceNote: adulting = googling basic tasks like a test you didn't study for; rewritten original reflective quote

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為大人什麼都會，長大才發現，所謂的大人，只是把 Google 開在另一個分頁，一邊查一邊點頭說「嗯我知道」。

報稅、換輪胎、通馬桶、跟房東吵架，沒有一項是天生就會的，全都是現學現賣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個昨天才偷偷 Google「洗衣機 E3 是什麼意思」的成熟大人
variations: 長大不是突然什麼都會了，是學會了一邊查一邊裝得很淡定。

en.content:
As a kid I thought grown-ups just knew things. Turns out being an adult is keeping Google open in another tab, nodding along and saying 'yeah, I know' while you frantically look it up.

Taxes, changing a tire, unclogging a drain, arguing with a landlord — nobody's born knowing any of it. You're learning it live.
en.editorNote: Send it to the 'grown-up' who secretly googled 'what does E3 mean on a washing machine' last night
variations: Growing up isn't suddenly knowing everything. It's learning to google it and look calm at the same time.

items.sourceNote: 年輕不懂低頭、長大才發現先低頭的人是贏家; rewritten original reflective quote

zh-tw.content:
年輕的時候覺得道歉很吃虧，低頭是輸，硬起來才叫有原則。

長大後才慢慢懂，先開口的那個人不是比較弱，是他比較想把事情解決，而不是把面子留到最後一刻。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了一口氣冷戰三天、其實心裡早就想和好的朋友
variations: 小時候以為贏就是不認錯。長大才發現，願意先伸手的人，通常才是那個更成熟的。

en.content:
When you're young, apologizing feels like losing. Backing down feels weak; digging in feels like having principles.

Growing up, you slowly get it: the person who speaks first isn't the weaker one. They just care more about fixing the problem than about saving face till the bitter end.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend giving someone the silent treatment for three days who secretly wanted to make up on day one
variations: As a kid, winning meant never admitting fault. As an adult, the one who reaches out first is usually the grown-up in the room.

items.sourceNote: adulting = tired, still responsible for everything; sick-day contrast; 初級大人 vs 高級大人; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
初級大人生病：燒到三十八度還是硬撐進公司，坐在位子上發抖，覺得請假很對不起大家。

高級大人生病：一句「我今天不舒服，請假一天」，然後把手機關靜音，安心睡到中午。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個感冒還在回訊息、把自己燃燒殆盡的工作狂
variations: 初級大人不舒服：先問「今天請假會不會很麻煩大家？」高級大人不舒服：先問「我要看哪一科？」

en.content:
Junior adult gets sick: drags themselves to the office at 100°F, shivering at their desk, feeling guilty for even thinking about calling out.

Senior adult gets sick: sends one 'not feeling well, taking the day,' silences the phone, and sleeps till noon guilt-free.
en.editorNote: Send it to the workaholic who's still answering messages with a fever, running themselves into the ground
variations: Junior adult feeling sick: 'Will taking the day off be a hassle for everyone?' Senior adult feeling sick: 'Okay, which doctor do I need to see?'

items.sourceNote: 成熟是雖然想追究但能夠不追究; rewritten original reflective quote

zh-tw.content:
年輕的時候，什麼都要爭個對錯，一句話沒說清楚就要對方道歉，覺得不追究到底就是委屈了自己。

長大後才慢慢懂，成熟不是什麼都不在乎，而是明明很想追究，最後卻選擇算了——不是原諒對方，是不想再讓一件小事，繼續佔用你本來就不多的力氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了一句話糾結一整晚、其實只是捨不得放過自己的朋友
variations: 小時候覺得放過別人是輸。長大才發現，願意先把這件事放下的人，其實是先讓自己自由。
成熟不是變得冷漠，是學會分辨哪些事值得認真，哪些事笑一笑就過去。

en.content:
When you're young, everything has to be settled. One unclear sentence and you need an apology; letting it slide feels like letting yourself get shortchanged.

Growing up, you slowly get it: maturity isn't not caring. It's wanting badly to make a point and then choosing to let it go anyway — not to forgive them, but to stop letting one small thing keep draining the energy you don't have much of to begin with.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who stews all night over one comment — really they just can't cut themselves loose
variations: As a kid, letting someone off felt like losing. As an adult, the one willing to drop it first is really just setting themselves free.
Maturity isn't going cold. It's learning which things deserve your full attention and which ones you can just laugh off.

items.sourceNote: being an adult = small unglamorous disasters strung together and called responsibility; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為長大是一件很有規劃、很體面的事：西裝筆挺、行程滿檔、一切盡在掌握。

長大後才發現，所謂的責任感，其實就是把一連串不起眼的小災難——水管漏了、發票要對了、車險快到期了、冰箱有東西過期了——串在一起，然後假裝很鎮定地一件一件處理完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個外表看起來很穩、其實每天都在滅火的成熟大人
variations: 當大人不是一直贏，是一直在處理一堆本來以為長大就不會遇到的麻煩。
所謂成熟，就是災難照樣一個接一個來，只是你臉上已經學會不動聲色。

en.content:
As a kid I thought being grown up would be an organized, dignified affair: sharp clothes, a full calendar, everything under control.

Growing up, you find out 'responsibility' is really just a string of small, unglamorous disasters — a leaking pipe, a receipt to reconcile, car insurance about to lapse, something expired in the fridge — lined up back to back, and you handling them one by one while pretending to be perfectly calm.
en.editorNote: Send it to the put-together adult who looks steady but is quietly putting out fires all day
variations: Being an adult isn't a winning streak. It's an endless queue of hassles you assumed you'd outgrow.
Maturity is the disasters still lining up one after another — you've just learned to keep a straight face.

items.sourceNote: junior vs senior adult contrast, handling a defective purchase / customer service; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
初級大人東西買到瑕疵：「算了啦，反正也才幾百塊，退貨還要跑一趟、打客服又要等，懶得處理。」

高級大人東西買到瑕疵：拍照、留單據、一通電話講清楚，該退的退、該換的換，全程不帶一點情緒。

差別不是計較，是知道自己的權益值得花那五分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個東西壞了只會嘆氣、從來不敢開口退換的爛好人
variations: 初級大人收到錯的餐點：默默吃完，還跟店員說謝謝。高級大人：當場禮貌反映，換一份對的。
長大就是慢慢學會，開口爭取不是丟臉，忍下來才是虧到自己。

en.content:
Junior adult gets a defective product: 'Forget it, it was only a few bucks. Returning it means another trip, calling support means waiting on hold — can't be bothered.'

Senior adult gets a defective product: takes photos, keeps the receipt, makes one clear call, gets the refund or replacement, all without a shred of drama.

The difference isn't being petty. It's knowing your rights are worth those five minutes.
en.editorNote: Send it to the pushover who just sighs when something breaks and never speaks up for a refund
variations: Junior adult gets the wrong order: eats it quietly and still thanks the server. Senior adult: politely flags it and gets the right one.
Growing up is slowly learning that speaking up isn't embarrassing — swallowing it is the thing that costs you.

items.sourceNote: self-investment guilt, paying for gym/courses/apps for an imagined better self; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
成年人的自我投資清單：辦了健身房會員、買了線上課程、下載了學語言的 app、囤了一整排看起來很勵志的書。

實際使用率：健身房去過兩次、課程停在第一集、app 只剩下每天提醒你「還沒學喔」、書用來墊螢幕高度。

所謂會員費，其實是繳給那個想像中更好的自己的贖罪券。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每年一月都要重新辦一次健身房、然後三月就消失的朋友
variations: 我不是在健身，我是在付錢請一間健身房，幫我保管我還想努力的那份幻想。
長大後最貴的消費，是為『我以後一定會用到』買單，然後從來沒用到。

en.content:
An adult's self-investment list: signed up for the gym, bought the online course, downloaded the language app, stacked a whole shelf of very inspiring books.

Actual usage: went to the gym twice, course stuck on episode one, app now just reminds you daily that you 'still haven't studied,' books used to prop up the monitor.

That membership fee is really an indulgence you pay to the better version of yourself you keep imagining.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who re-joins the gym every January and vanishes by March
variations: I'm not working out. I'm paying a gym to safekeep my fantasy that I still plan to try.
The priciest adult purchase is paying for 'I'll definitely use this someday' and then never using it.

items.sourceNote: junior vs senior adult, handling an unexpected expense / emergency fund; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
初級大人遇到意外支出（手機摔壞、突然要看牙、車子進廠）：整個月的預算瞬間崩盤，開始煩惱接下來三週要靠泡麵撐。

高級大人遇到意外支出：淡定從那筆「反正人生一定會出包」的預備金裡拿出來，付完連眉頭都沒皺一下。

長大就是，慢慢學會替那些你還不知道會發生的倒楣事，先存好一筆錢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次一有突發花費就開始盤算要吃土的月光族朋友
variations: 初級大人的存款：一次意外就見底。高級大人的存款：有一格是專門用來接住意外的。
真正的安全感，不是戶頭數字多大，是知道臨時出事的時候，你扛得住。

en.content:
Junior adult hits an unexpected expense (cracked phone, sudden dental visit, car in the shop): the whole month's budget collapses instantly, and you start dreading three weeks of instant noodles.

Senior adult hits an unexpected expense: calmly pulls from the 'life will definitely throw a curveball' fund, pays, and doesn't even flinch.

Growing up is slowly learning to set money aside for the bad luck you don't even know is coming yet.
en.editorNote: Send it to the paycheck-to-paycheck friend who starts bracing for ramen season the moment anything unexpected pops up
variations: Junior adult's savings: one surprise drains it. Senior adult's savings: has a slot built just to catch surprises.
Real security isn't how big the number is. It's knowing that when something breaks, you can take the hit.

items.sourceNote: 115年5-6月統一發票 7/25 開獎新聞；改寫成初級/高級大人對照原創，發票對獎主題在本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
初級大人對發票：發票塞在包包底層、外套口袋、桌上那疊紙裡，開獎過了三天才想起來，翻出來的時候有一半已經跟衣服一起洗成紙漿。

高級大人對發票：早就全部存進手機載具，開獎當天 app 自己跳通知，中兩百塊還會截圖傳到群組炫耀一下。

大人的期待其實很好懂：兩個月一次，希望自己是那個花一百五十塊、卻抱走一千萬的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 每逢開獎日隔天丟到群組，那個還在翻外套口袋的朋友一定會跳出來認領
variations: 長大後才知道，人生最刺激的抽獎不是演唱會門票，是每兩個月一次、獎金兩百塊的那一種。
沒中也沒關係，那疊發票至少證明這兩個月你有好好吃飯、好好過日子。

en.content:
Junior adult and the receipt draw: receipts stuffed in the bottom of the bag, in jacket pockets, in that pile on the desk. You remember three days after the numbers are out, and half of what you find already went through the wash.

Senior adult and the receipt draw: everything saved to the phone wallet, the app pings you on draw day by itself, and winning the smallest prize still earns a screenshot in the group chat.

Adult hope is a simple thing: once every two months, wanting to be the person who spent five bucks and walked away with the jackpot.
en.editorNote: Post it the day after any draw and the friend still digging through coat pockets will out themselves
variations: Turns out the most thrilling lottery in adult life isn't concert tickets. It's the one that pays out pocket change every two months.
Not winning is fine. That stack of receipts is proof you ate, paid your way, and got through two months.

items.sourceNote: 2026 颱風季報導；改寫成原創「以為長大後」語錄，颱風假主題在本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
小時候聽到颱風要來，整晚都在偷看氣象報告，希望它再靠近一點，最好剛好落在上課那天。

長大後聽到颱風要來，腦中跑的是：陽台的東西收了沒、水夠不夠、會不會停電、冰箱那些菜怎麼辦，還有——就算停班，會議還是會改成線上開。

颱風假沒有消失，它只是從一份禮物，變成一件要處理的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 警報一發布就丟到群組，保證一票人回「有夠寫實」
variations: 小時候希望颱風轉過來，長大後希望它轉開，中間隔的不是幾年，是幾份責任。
大人的颱風夜，不是在等停課通知，是在確認家裡每個人都好好的。

en.content:
As a kid, a storm warning meant refreshing the forecast all night, quietly hoping it would swing a little closer and land right on a school day.

As an adult, a storm warning means: did I bring the balcony stuff in, is there enough water, what if the power cuts out, what happens to everything in the fridge — and even if the office closes, the meeting just moves online.

The storm day never disappeared. It just stopped being a gift and became one more thing to handle.
en.editorNote: Post it the moment a warning drops and watch everyone reply "too real"
variations: As a kid you hoped the storm would turn toward you. Now you hope it turns away. What's in between isn't years, it's responsibilities.
A grown-up storm night isn't about waiting for the cancellation notice. It's about checking that everyone at home is okay.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 熱浪與高溫新聞；改寫成初級/高級大人對照原創，防曬與熱傷害主題在本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
初級大人的夏天：三十八度照樣說走就走，防曬忘了擦、水也沒帶，回到家整個人像剛從烤箱端出來，還要跟自己說「我只是有點累」。

高級大人的夏天：出門前先看體感溫度，包包裡有水壺、防曬和一頂帽子，走路自動挑有騎樓的那一側，還會回頭提醒同事「記得喝水」。

不是變得龜毛，是身體終於教會你一件事：逞強沒有獎品。
zh-tw.editorNote: 熱到快融化的那幾天丟到辦公室群組，順便逼大家去裝水
variations: 長大後最實用的技能之一，是學會怎麼在大太陽底下不把自己搞垮。
小時候覺得撐傘很孬，長大後才知道，那叫做願意照顧自己。

en.content:
Junior adult in a heatwave: walks straight out into triple digits, no sunscreen, no water, comes home looking like something pulled out of an oven, and calls it "just a little tired."

Senior adult in a heatwave: checks the heat index first, packs a bottle, sunscreen, and a hat, automatically walks on the shaded side of the street, and turns around to tell a coworker to drink something.

It isn't fussiness. Your body finally taught you that toughing it out comes with no prize.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the work chat on a scorching day and make everyone go refill their bottle
variations: One of the most useful adult skills is knowing how not to wreck yourself in the sun.
As a kid, carrying shade around felt embarrassing. Now it just means you're willing to look after yourself.

items.sourceNote: 成年人日常體貼主題；原創的博愛座／讓座角度，本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
初級大人在車廂裡：低頭滑手機、假裝沒看到，心裡默默祈禱下一站有人先站起來。

高級大人在車廂裡：一上車就站在門邊，因為站著就不用糾結，位子留給更需要的人，自己也懶得再演那齣戲。

長大有一部分是這樣的——你不再花力氣裝作沒看見，因為誠實其實比較省力。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次通勤都要跟自己內心天人交戰的朋友
variations: 大人的體貼不是很會講話，是很會看見別人需要什麼。
位子讓出去的那一秒你會發現，站著沒有你想像中那麼累。

en.content:
Junior adult on a packed train: head down, scrolling, pretending not to notice, quietly praying somebody else stands up at the next stop.

Senior adult on a packed train: stands by the door from the start, because standing means never having to agonize, the seat goes to whoever needs it, and you're too tired to keep performing.

Part of growing up is this — you stop spending energy pretending not to see, because honesty turns out to be the cheaper option.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who fights a whole moral battle every single commute
variations: Adult kindness isn't saying the right thing. It's noticing what someone actually needs.
The second you give the seat up, you realize standing was never as bad as you'd built it up to be.

items.sourceNote: modern adulting preparedness theme；原創的手機電量／行動電源角度，本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
初級大人的手機電量：出門前 43%，覺得應該夠，中午剩 8%，開始在咖啡廳裡用眼神搜尋插座，像在尋寶。

高級大人的手機電量：出門前充飽，包包裡永遠躺著一顆行動電源跟一條線，還會順口問旁邊的人「你要不要充？」

長大不是突然變得很有本事，是慢慢學會把「等一下可能會需要」提前準備好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次見面手機電量都是紅色的朋友
variations: 成年人的安全感之一，是知道那條線已經在包包裡了。
小時候覺得帶一堆東西出門很麻煩，長大後才懂，那叫做不想再狼狽第二次。

en.content:
Junior adult's battery: 43% heading out the door, figures that's plenty, down to 8% by lunch, scanning the cafe walls for an outlet like it's a treasure hunt.

Senior adult's battery: charged before leaving, a power bank and a cable permanently living in the bag, and a casual "want a charge?" for whoever's nearby.

Growing up isn't suddenly becoming capable. It's slowly learning to handle "I might need this later" ahead of time.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend whose phone is in the red every time you meet up
variations: One quiet adult comfort is knowing the cable is already in the bag.
As a kid, hauling stuff around felt like a hassle. Now it just means you'd rather not get stranded twice.

items.sourceNote: burnout 主題的成年人笑話彙整（「adulthood is multiple crises, concurrently」）；原創的「草稿匣裡的辭職信」角度，本檔尚未出現

zh-tw.content:
我的辭職信已經在草稿匣裡住了兩年。

每次開完一場莫名其妙的會，我就打開它加一句；遇到還算過得去的一週，又默默刪掉兩行。它現在是第十七個版本，寫得比我交出去的任何一份報告都認真。

我沒有要寄出去。它不是出口，是止痛藥——知道那個東西還在，我今天才有辦法再坐回位子上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個電腦裡有一個資料夾叫「備用」的同事，不用多說，他會懂
variations: 大人的勇氣不一定是遞出那封信，有時候是每天重新決定先不遞。
二十五歲想離職，靠的是一股氣；三十五歲想離職，要先算存款可以撐幾個月。

en.content:
My resignation letter has been living in my drafts folder for two years.

Every pointless meeting, I open it and add a line. Every week that turns out okay, I quietly delete two. It's on version seventeen now, and it's better written than anything I've actually turned in.

I'm not going to send it. It isn't an exit, it's a painkiller. Knowing it's still in there is what gets me back into the chair.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker with a folder on their desktop named "just in case" — no explanation needed
variations: Adult courage isn't always sending the letter. Some days it's deciding, one more time, not to.
At 25 you quit on a feeling. At 35 you quit on a spreadsheet that tells you how many months you can last.

items.sourceNote: 成年人消費／購物慾主題的英文笑話彙整；原創的「除濕機與耗材」購物車角度，與既有的家電規格研究梗不同

zh-tw.content:
我購物車最上面那幾樣：一台除濕機、五包濾心、一組耐熱玻璃保鮮盒，還有一支可以刷到浴室縫隙的細刷。

二十歲的我看到這張清單，大概會以為帳號被盜了。

慾望其實沒有變小，它只是換了方向——現在讓我心跳加速的，不是能讓今天很開心的東西，是能讓明天的我少做一件事的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個生日禮物許願要氣炸鍋、而且是認真的朋友
variations: 大人版的衝動購物：半夜兩點下訂一台除濕機，隔天醒來完全不後悔。
真正長大的徵兆，是你開始覺得「耗材」這兩個字有點浪漫。

en.content:
Top of my cart right now: a dehumidifier, a five-pack of filter cartridges, a set of heatproof glass containers, and a brush skinny enough to reach the grout in the shower.

If twenty-year-old me saw this list, he'd assume the account got hacked.

The wanting never shrank. It just changed direction. What gets my heart going now isn't something that makes today fun. It's something that saves tomorrow-me one job.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who asked for an air fryer as a birthday present and meant it
variations: Adult impulse buying: ordering a dehumidifier at 2 a.m. and waking up with zero regrets.
You know you've grown up when the word "refills" starts to sound a little romantic.

items.sourceNote: relatable adulting jokes 彙整（租屋、生活開銷主題）；原創的「退租押金」角度，本檔的房租相關內容都沒碰過搬走那天

zh-tw.content:
退租那天，我跪在地上刷一道我搬進來就已經在那裡的水漬。

房東拿著手電筒照牆角，我拿著抹布跟在後面，兩個人像在演一齣沒有台詞的戲。最後他說「押金三天內匯給你」，我在門口跟他道謝，聲音還抖了一下。

沒有人事先告訴你，長大會包含這一段：為了那筆錢，你會把一間自己正在離開的房子，擦得比搬進來的時候還乾淨。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個下個月要搬家、已經開始在陽台堆紙箱的朋友
variations: 大人的儀式感之一：把鑰匙交出去之前，回頭看一眼那個空掉的房間。
押金匯進來的那天，你會發現自己有點捨不得——捨不得的不是房子，是住在那裡的那幾年的自己。

en.content:
Move-out day, and there I am on my knees scrubbing a water stain that was already there the day I signed the lease.

The landlord walks the corners with a flashlight, I follow behind with a rag, and the two of us perform a play with no lines. He says the deposit will be wired within three days, and I thank him at the door with a small wobble in my voice.

Nobody warns you this part is included: for that money, you'll leave a place cleaner than you found it — a place you're leaving anyway.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend moving next month who has already started stacking boxes on the balcony
variations: One quiet adult ritual: one last look at the empty room before you hand over the keys.
The day the deposit lands, you notice you miss something. Not the apartment — the version of you who lived there.

items.sourceNote: 「三十歲之後沒人警告你的事」網友串，其中一條是 the people you work with keep getting younger；改寫成台灣職場的新同事情境，本檔沒有同類角度

zh-tw.content:
今天帶新同事熟悉環境，聊到一半他說：「我是去年畢業的。」

我在心裡默默算了一下，發現我開始上班那一年，他還在唸國中。

然後我聽見自己說出那句這輩子最不想說的話：「我們以前不是這樣做的。」

沒有人通知你哪一天會被換到另一邊，你只是某天開口，就發現自己已經站在那裡了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近開始帶人、還沒準備好被叫「前輩」的朋友
variations: 長大最安靜的一刻，是你發現辦公室裡最會用新工具的人不是你了，而你居然鬆了一口氣。
以前怕被當成菜鳥，現在怕被當成那個很難溝通的老鳥。

en.content:
I was showing the new hire around today, and halfway through he mentioned he graduated last year.

I did the math in my head and realized that when I started this job, he was in middle school.

Then I heard myself say the sentence I swore I'd never say: "That's not how we used to do it."

Nobody tells you which day you get moved to the other side. You just open your mouth one morning and find you're already standing there.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who just started managing people and isn't ready to be the veteran yet
variations: The quietest sign of getting older: you're no longer the one who figures out the new software first, and you're weirdly relieved about it.
I used to worry about being seen as the rookie. Now I worry about being the one nobody wants to explain things to.

items.sourceNote: 來源梗：adulthood isn't one crisis after another, it's multiple crises concurrently；改寫成「危機不排隊」的台灣生活版本

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為麻煩會排隊：一件解決了，下一件才會進來。

實際上它們是一起來的。冷氣壞掉的那天，剛好是報告要交、車子要保養、家裡打電話說要帶長輩去複診的同一天。

大人不是比較會處理問題，只是習慣了同時有五件事都還沒解決，還能把飯吃完、把澡洗完、然後睡著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個這禮拜已經被三件事同時追著跑的朋友
variations: 成年人的日常不是闖關，是同時開著五個分頁，每一個都在轉圈圈。
以前以為長大會變得比較從容，後來才知道那個從容，只是習慣了亂。

en.content:
As a kid I assumed problems formed an orderly line: solve one, then the next one steps up.

They don't. The AC dies on the same day the report is due, the car needs servicing, and someone calls to say a follow-up appointment got moved to tomorrow.

Adults aren't better at solving things. We've just gotten used to having five unfinished problems at once and still managing to eat dinner, take a shower, and fall asleep.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who's been chased by three separate deadlines all week
variations: Adult life isn't levels you clear. It's five browser tabs open, all of them still loading.
I thought growing up meant getting calmer. Turns out the calm is just familiarity with the mess.

items.sourceNote: 網友分享「沒人幫你準備好的大人問題」，含親子角色互換；改寫成家庭群組裡「提問方變回答方」的台灣情境

zh-tw.content:
家庭群組裡，以前發問的那個人是我：這個表怎麼填、這個要找誰、這個能不能吃。

不知道從哪一年開始，訊息的方向反過來了。爸媽拍一張看不懂的通知單傳進來，後面加一句「你有空的時候看一下就好」。

那句「有空的時候」讓我鼻子一酸。他們不是不急，是怕麻煩你。

所以我現在都盡量先回。不是因為我變厲害了，是因為輪到我了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近開始幫爸媽處理各種文件、還沒對別人講過這件事的朋友
variations: 長大的分界線，是家庭群組裡那個負責查資料的人換成了你。
以前是「媽，這個怎麼辦」，現在是「你放著，我來處理」——同一個群組，位置換了。

en.content:
In the family group chat, I used to be the one asking: how do I fill this out, who do I call, is this still safe to eat.

Somewhere along the way the messages reversed direction. Now my parents send a photo of a notice they can't parse, with a line underneath: "Whenever you have time, no rush."

That "no rush" is what gets me. It isn't that it can wait. It's that they don't want to be a bother.

So I answer fast now. Not because I got competent. Because it's my turn.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who quietly started handling their parents' paperwork this year
variations: You know you've grown up when you're the one who looks things up for the family chat.
It went from "Mom, what do I do about this?" to "Leave it, I'll take care of it." Same chat, different seat.

items.sourceNote: hard adulting truths 一文提到社群比較造成的落差感；改寫成深夜滑手機的具體場景，本檔沒有社群比較主題

zh-tw.content:
晚上十一點半，我端著一碗隨便煮的麵坐在沙發上滑手機。

螢幕裡的人在升職、在裝潢新家、在某個看起來很涼的地方拍海。每一則都短短的，每一則看起來都像是「我已經想清楚了」。

後來我才慢慢懂：那些是別人剪好的三十秒，我看的是自己沒剪過的一整天。

拿一整天去跟三十秒比，本來就不會贏。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個滑完限時動態就開始懷疑自己的朋友
variations: 別人的生活是預告片，你的是完整版——連中間發呆的那四十分鐘都留著。
深夜的手機有一種魔法：能把所有人的好日子，剛好排在你最累的那一天給你看。

en.content:
Eleven thirty at night, a bowl of whatever-noodles on my lap, thumb scrolling.

Everyone on the screen is getting promoted, renovating a place, filming the ocean somewhere breezy. Every clip is short. Every clip looks like someone who has it figured out.

It took me a while to get it: those are other people's edited thirty seconds, and I'm watching my own unedited whole day.

A whole day was never going to beat thirty seconds.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who closes the app feeling worse than when they opened it
variations: Their life is the trailer. Yours is the full cut, including the forty minutes you spent staring at the wall.
Late-night phones have a talent for showing you everyone's best day on the night you had your worst.

items.sourceNote: adulting meme 集錦裡常見「長大就是自己修東西」的梗；改寫成螺絲起子與蹲下來看一眼的具體場景，本檔沒有工具箱主題

zh-tw.content:
小時候家裡有東西壞掉，我的維修策略只有一招：大喊「爸——」。

現在我會先蹲下來看一眼，然後從抽屜裡抽出十字起子，而且順手就挑了中號的那支。

不是因為我很會修，是因為那年有一個下午，家裡沒有人可以喊，我只好自己蹲下去看。

長大的證據不是你會修，是你願意先蹲下來看一眼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給第一次自己換燈泡、鎖門把、通水管的朋友
variations: 大人的成就感很廉價：一顆螺絲鎖回去，就覺得自己撐得起整個家。
從家裡沒有起子，到家裡有三種尺寸的起子，中間隔的不是錢，是好幾次「看來只能自己來了」。

en.content:
When something broke at my house as a kid, my entire repair strategy was yelling "Daaad."

Now I crouch down, take a look, and pull the medium Phillips head out of the drawer without even thinking about it.

I'm not handy. It's just that one afternoon there was nobody left to yell for, so I crouched down and looked.

Proof that you grew up isn't that you can fix it. It's that you're willing to look at it first.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just changed a light bulb without calling anyone about it
variations: Adult wins come cheap: one screw back in place and suddenly you can hold up an entire household.
Going from owning no screwdriver to owning three sizes of screwdriver doesn't cost money. It costs a few rounds of "guess it's me, then."

items.sourceNote: 2026 版 adult humor 整理提到 always-on burnout 的主題；改寫成「洗完澡還留著上班的味道」，本檔沒有下班後切不掉工作模式的角度

zh-tw.content:
晚上八點到家，澡洗了，衣服換了，可是我知道自己身上還留著一股上班的味道。

洗不掉的那種。它會讓你在洗碗洗到一半突然想起明天要回的那封信，會讓你在滑影片的時候，用看報表的表情看一隻貓。

以前以為下班是一個時間點，後來才發現下班是一段路，而且大部分人都走到一半就睡著了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在那個「明明已經放假卻放不掉」的群組裡
variations: 身體六點就離開公司了，腦袋大概十一點半才慢慢跟上來。
真正的休息不是不做事，是終於不用在心裡預演明天的對話。

en.content:
Home by eight. Showered, changed, and I can still tell the workday hasn't come off me.

Not the kind that washes off. It's why an unanswered email surfaces halfway through the dishes, and why I watch a cat video with my spreadsheet face on.

I used to think clocking out was a moment. Turns out it's a walk home, and most of us fall asleep partway through it.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the group chat where everyone is technically off work
variations: My body left the office at six. My head caught up somewhere around eleven thirty.
Real rest isn't doing nothing. It's finally not rehearsing tomorrow's conversation in your head.

items.sourceNote: relatable memes 提到成年友情從夜衝變成群組低頻互動；改寫成團購「+1」的台灣日常場景，本檔沒有團購主題

zh-tw.content:
大學的時候，友情是半夜兩點有人敲你的門說：「走啦，出去。」

現在，友情是群組裡有人丟一句：「衛生紙特價，要的+1。」

然後五個人在三十秒內排隊+1。沒有人問彼此最近好不好，可是每個人都知道：這群人還在。

大人的感情很省話，但很準時。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個平常已讀不回、只有團購才會冒泡的老朋友
variations: 我們已經很久沒有聊過心事了，但我知道他冰箱裡那瓶醬油是我揪的那批。
大人的「我想你了」翻成日常語是：「這個我順便幫你買一份喔？」

en.content:
In college, friendship was someone banging on your door at 2 a.m. saying "get up, we're going out."

Now friendship is someone dropping a line in the group chat: "toilet paper's on sale, say +1 if you want in."

Five people +1 within thirty seconds. Nobody asks how anyone's holding up, and somehow everyone knows: this crew is still here.

Grown-up affection uses fewer words, but it shows up on time.
en.editorNote: Send it to the old friend who only surfaces for group orders
variations: We haven't talked about anything real in months, but I know the soy sauce in his fridge came from a batch I organized.
"I miss you," translated into adult, is: "want me to grab you one while I'm at it?"

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常拿「大人囤日用品」當笑點；改寫成備用電池與燈泡的安全感描寫，本檔沒有常備品／囤貨主題

zh-tw.content:
我最近發現一件事：讓我半夜睡得著的，不是存款的數字，是我知道抽屜裡有兩顆三號電池、櫃子上有一顆備用燈泡。

小時候覺得那種什麼都要囤一份的大人很無聊。長大才懂那不是無聊，那是有人曾經在半夜遇過整間房突然黑掉，然後默默決定：以後不要再遇到第二次。

安全感不是什麼很大的東西。大部分的夜裡，它只有一顆電池那麼大。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配一張自己那個整齊到有點可疑的備品抽屜照片
variations: 大人的浪漫是：東西還沒壞，我就先把下一個買好放著了。
以前買東西問的是「我想要嗎」，現在買東西問的是「壞掉的那天，我來不來得及」。

en.content:
Here's what I figured out lately: the thing that lets me sleep at night isn't the number in my account. It's knowing there are two spare AAs in the drawer and one spare bulb on the shelf.

As a kid I thought adults who stockpiled things were boring. Turns out it isn't boring. It's someone who once stood in a room that went dark at midnight and quietly decided: not twice.

Security isn't a big thing. Most nights it's about the size of one battery.
en.editorNote: Pairs well with a photo of your suspiciously organized supply drawer
variations: Adult romance is buying the replacement before the original breaks.
I used to ask "do I want this?" Now I ask "on the day it dies, will I be ready?"

items.sourceNote: 2026 中元普渡懶人包（鬼門開 8/13、中元節 8/27）提到公司普渡的採買與流程；改寫成「小時候搶供品 vs 長大負責結帳」，本檔沒有普渡／供品主題

zh-tw.content:
小時候最期待普渡：供桌上那堆零食，拜完就變成全家可以合法搬走的寶藏。我還會偷偷把自己想吃的那包擺到最前面，讓神明先看到。

今年普渡，我是那個推著推車在賣場繞第三圈的人。挑好拜的、好分的、真的有人會吃的，算人數、算預算，結帳的時候看一眼金額，心裡默默補了一句：保佑我。

長大不是不再期待那些零食，是你終於知道，那堆零食一直都是有人先掏錢買的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 農曆七月採買前貼到家庭群組或公司群組，配一張推車的照片剛剛好
variations: 以前拜拜是等著吃，現在拜拜是先付款、再擺盤、最後負責把沒人拿的那箱搬回家。
供桌上那包我最想吃的零食，現在隨時買得起了，只是也沒有那麼好吃了。

en.content:
As a kid, offering season was the best part of the year. Everything on the table turned into snacks the whole family could legally raid afterward, and I'd sneak my favorite bag to the front so the spirits would notice it first.

This year I'm the one pushing a cart through the store on lap three, picking what displays well, splits evenly, and someone will actually eat. Counting heads, counting budget. At checkout I looked at the total and quietly added: bless me too.

Growing up doesn't mean you stopped wanting the snacks. It means you finally know somebody paid for them first.
en.editorNote: For the group chat right before the shopping run, with a photo of the cart
variations: Rituals used to mean waiting to eat. Now they mean paying first, arranging the plate, and carrying home the box nobody picked.
I can buy that one snack I always wanted whenever I feel like it now. Turns out it doesn't taste the same.

items.sourceNote: 2026 鬼門開 8/13 與農曆七月禁忌整理；改寫成「傳統禁忌 vs 大人自己的禁忌」對照，本檔沒有禁忌主題

zh-tw.content:
農曆七月的禁忌我從小背到大：晚上不要曬衣服、不要拍別人的肩膀、不要在半夜叫人全名。

長大以後我有了自己的一套：睡前不要點開工作群組、月底不要打開信用卡帳單、凌晨三點不要把銀行 App 叫出來看。

鬼門開一個月就關了，我這幾條禁忌是全年無休。
zh-tw.editorNote: 鬼門開那幾天發，配一張深夜還亮著的手機螢幕最有畫面
variations: 真正會嚇到我的東西從來不挑農曆七月，它一年三百六十五天都在上班。
小時候怕的是走廊傳來的聲音，現在怕的是手機在半夜亮起來。

en.content:
I grew up memorizing the Ghost Month rules: don't hang laundry after dark, don't tap anyone on the shoulder, don't call out a person's full name at night.

These days I keep my own list: don't open the work chat before bed, don't open the credit card statement at the end of the month, don't open the banking app at three in the morning.

The ghost gate shuts after a month. My rules run all year.
en.editorNote: Post it the week Ghost Month starts, with a photo of a phone lighting up at night
variations: The stuff that actually scares me doesn't wait for one month a year. It clocks in every single day.
As a kid I was scared of noises in the hallway. Now I'm scared of my phone lighting up at 2 a.m.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常見「大人買文具說服自己會改變」的梗；改寫成台灣八月底文具店開學專區的場景，本檔沒有文具／筆記本主題

zh-tw.content:
八月底走進文具店，開學專區已經擺出來了。

我早就沒有開學這件事了，可是我還是在那排筆記本前面站了十分鐘，翻了三本，最後帶走一本有格線的。

回家寫了兩頁，第三頁空白到今天。

大人買的從來不是筆記本，是「從下禮拜一開始，我會變成另一個人」的那一點點可能。而且說真的，一百二十塊買這個，很划算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個抽屜裡躺著五本只寫過前兩頁的筆記本的朋友
variations: 我家有五本只寫到第二頁的筆記本，那是我認真想把生活重來五次的證據。
大人的新年不在一月，在任何一個你剛買完新筆記本的星期天晚上。

en.content:
Walked into a stationery store in late August and the back-to-school display was already up.

I haven't had a first day of school in years. I still stood in front of the notebooks for ten minutes, flipped through three, and left with a lined one.

Filled two pages at home. Page three has been blank ever since.

Adults aren't buying a notebook. We're buying the small chance that starting Monday we'll be a different person. And honestly, four bucks for that is a bargain.
en.editorNote: For the friend with five barely-used notebooks in a drawer
variations: I own five notebooks with two pages filled. That's five separate times I meant to restart my whole life.
An adult's new year isn't in January. It's any Sunday night right after buying a fresh notebook.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常見「第一次被叫 sir／ma'am」的梗；改寫成台灣電梯裡遇到鄰居小孩的場景，本檔沒有被稱呼叔叔阿姨的主題

zh-tw.content:
上禮拜在電梯遇到鄰居的小孩，他很有禮貌地按著開門鍵，說：「叔叔先請。」

我愣了兩秒。不是不能接受，是那一秒我腦中閃過的畫面，是十歲的我，對某個大人說過一模一樣的話。當時我完全沒覺得那個人老，我只覺得他是大人，他什麼都知道。

原來長大不是變老，是有一天你走到了另一邊，然後發現這一邊的人也沒有準備好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合第一次被叫叔叔或阿姨的那天發，收留一下當下的心情
variations: 我不是介意被叫阿姨，我只是突然想起自己也曾經站在那個孩子的位置。
那個小孩看我的眼神，跟我當年看大人的眼神一樣：以為我什麼都知道。

en.content:
Ran into a neighbor's kid in the elevator last week. He held the door open, very politely, and said, "After you, sir."

I froze for two seconds. Not offended, exactly. It's that in that second I saw myself at ten, saying the exact same thing to some adult. I never thought that person was old. I just thought they were a grown-up, and grown-ups knew things.

Turns out growing up isn't aging. It's the day you end up on the other side and find out nobody over here was ready either.
en.editorNote: For the day someone calls you sir or ma'am for the very first time
variations: It's not that I mind being called ma'am. It's that I suddenly remembered standing exactly where that kid was standing.
That kid looked at me the way I used to look at adults: like I had all of it figured out.

items.sourceNote: adulting 相關討論常提到成年後友情的形式轉變；改寫成台灣「我順路」這句客套話背後的溫柔，本檔沒有順路／繞路接送的主題

zh-tw.content:
「我順路。」

這三個字大概是成年人最常說的謊。

上禮拜下大雨，朋友傳訊息說他順路載我一段。後來我點開地圖才發現，他從他家過來要繞二十分鐘，送完我回去再二十分鐘。

成年人的時間是拿命換的，一天裡沒有一分鐘是多出來的。所以當有人願意從自己的人生裡挖四十分鐘給你，還輕描淡寫地說一句「反正我順路」——

那不是順路，那是他把你排進了他的路線裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是說「我順路」的朋友，讓他知道你其實查過地圖
variations: 「反正我順路」是成年人版本的「我很在乎你」，只是直接講出來太害羞。
後來我也開始對別人說順路了。地圖知道我在說謊，但我不打算承認。

en.content:
"I was heading that way anyway."

Probably the most common lie adults tell.

It poured last week and a friend texted that he'd swing by and grab me since he was passing through. I pulled up the map later. His place is twenty minutes the wrong direction, and another twenty back after dropping me off.

Adults pay for time with their lives. There isn't a spare minute in the day. So when someone carves forty of them out of their own life for you and shrugs it off with "it was on my way" —

it wasn't on their way. They put you on it.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who always claims they were in the neighborhood anyway
variations: "It was on my way" is the adult version of "I care about you," just too shy to say it straight.
These days I say it to other people too. The map knows I'm lying. I'm not planning to admit it.

items.sourceNote: 「討厭其實很耗體力，我們並沒有憎恨那麼多事物的能力」的觀點；改寫成加班／打卡的比喻，本檔沒有「記恨很累」的主題

zh-tw.content:
二十幾歲的時候，我可以討厭一個人討厭一整年。

記得他講過的每一句話、他的語氣、他當下的表情，在腦裡一遍一遍重播，愈想愈氣，愈氣愈清醒。

現在不行了。討厭到第三天我就開始覺得累——原來記恨是要自己扛的。那個人早就下班回家吃飯睡覺了，只有我一個人還在加班。

所以我就放下了。不是原諒，也不是我變寬容，是我的力氣不夠分給那麼多人。

成年人的溫柔，有一大半其實是體力不足。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給還在為某個人生氣、氣到睡不著的朋友
variations: 我沒有原諒他，我只是有一天忘記要繼續討厭他了。
討厭一個人就是加班，沒有加班費，而且整間辦公室只有你在打卡。

en.content:
In my twenties I could resent someone for a solid year.

Every line they said, the tone, the exact look on their face, replayed on a loop until I was too angry to sleep.

I can't do it anymore. By day three of hating someone I just get tired. Turns out a grudge is something you carry alone. That person clocked out, went home, ate dinner, slept fine. I was the only one still working late.

So I let it go. Not forgiveness, not some new generosity of spirit. I just don't have enough energy to spread across that many people.

Half of what looks like adult grace is really just running low.
en.editorNote: For the friend still lying awake angry at someone
variations: I never forgave him. I just forgot to keep hating him one day.
Holding a grudge is unpaid overtime, and you're the only one who clocked in.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常見「沒有人在監督你」的梗；改寫成「自由的意思是要當自己的家長」，本檔沒有這個角度

zh-tw.content:
長大之後最可怕的，不是有人管你，是沒有人管你。

沒有人會問你今天有沒有吃到青菜，沒有人會提醒你藥還剩幾顆、上次量血壓是哪一年，也沒有人會在十一點半站在房門口說「該睡了」。

想幾點睡就幾點睡，想吃什麼就吃什麼。這就是你小時候拼命想要的那種自由。

只是沒有人先告訴你，自由的意思是：從今天起，你要當自己的家長。

而說真的，我這個家長，常常很不負責任。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給一個人住、晚餐常常配餅乾解決的那個朋友
variations: 自由的意思是沒有人會來收作業，也沒有人會來檢查你今天到底有沒有睡。
我當自己的小孩非常稱職，當自己的家長就很勉強。

en.content:
The scary part of growing up isn't having someone on your case. It's having nobody on your case.

No one asks whether you ate a vegetable today. No one reminds you how many pills are left in the bottle, or when you last had your blood pressure checked. No one stands in your doorway at 11:30 and says it's time to sleep.

Sleep whenever. Eat whatever. This is exactly the freedom you begged for as a kid.

Nobody mentioned that freedom means you're the parent now.

And honestly? I'm a pretty negligent one.
en.editorNote: For the friend living alone whose dinner is often just crackers
variations: Freedom means nobody collects your homework and nobody checks whether you slept.
I'm an excellent child to myself. As a parent to myself I'm barely passing.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常見「停好車後在車上多坐一下」的梗；改寫成台灣機車停在樓下滑手機十分鐘的場景，本檔沒有這個主題

zh-tw.content:
騎車回到家樓下，車停好了，安全帽也脫了，但我沒有上樓。

我就坐在機車上滑手機，滑一些根本沒在看的東西，滑了十分鐘。

樓上不是什麼可怕的地方，公司也沒有人在等我回訊息。我只是需要一段沒有人需要我的時間——不用當誰的同事、不用當誰的家人，就只是一個坐在車上的人。

成年人不是不想回家，是需要一小段在門外的時間，把身上那件「我很好」的外套先脫下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每天都比預期晚十分鐘才進家門的人
variations: 那十分鐘我什麼都沒做，但那是我一天裡唯一沒有身分的十分鐘。
不是不想上樓，是需要先在門外把表情調整好。

en.content:
Got home, parked, took off my helmet, and didn't go upstairs.

I sat there on the scooter scrolling through things I wasn't actually reading. Ten minutes.

Upstairs isn't a bad place. Nobody at work is waiting on a reply. I just needed a stretch of time where nobody needed me — not somebody's coworker, not somebody's family, just a person sitting on a parked bike.

Adults aren't avoiding home. We just need a few minutes outside the door to take off the jacket that says "I'm fine."
en.editorNote: For the person who walks in the door ten minutes later than expected, every single day
variations: I did nothing with those ten minutes, and they were the only ten minutes all day where I wasn't anyone.
It's not that I don't want to come in. I need a minute out here to fix my face first.

items.sourceNote: adulting 討論常提到「填表格才發現自己已經是大人」的時刻；改寫成台灣健檢表上緊急聯絡人欄位的角度，本檔沒有緊急聯絡人主題

zh-tw.content:
醫院的表格上有一欄叫「緊急聯絡人」。

以前那一欄我從來不用想，寫媽媽的名字，寫她的手機號碼，寫完就交出去。

上個月做健檢，筆停在那一格上，我想了大概十秒鐘。她已經六十幾歲了，真的有什麼事，第一個要通知的是她嗎？她接到那通電話，能做什麼？

最後我寫了另一個名字。

長大不是你終於有能力照顧誰了，是有一天你發現，那個一直被你寫在那一格的人，也需要有人保護。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個開始幫爸媽掛號、陪爸媽聽報告的朋友
variations: 那一格從一個名字換成另一個名字，中間隔了我整個二十幾歲。
以前寫緊急聯絡人，是想誰能救我；現在寫，是想誰不該先被嚇到。

en.content:
There's a line on every hospital form: emergency contact.

I never used to think about it. Mom's name, Mom's number, hand it in.

Last month at a checkup my pen stopped on that line for about ten seconds. She's in her sixties now. If something actually happened, is she the first person who should get that call? What could she do with it?

I wrote down a different name.

Growing up isn't finally being able to take care of someone. It's the day you notice that the person you'd been writing on that line needs somebody looking out for her too.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's started booking their parents' appointments and sitting in on the results
variations: That line went from one name to another name, and my entire twenties happened in between.
I used to write down whoever could rescue me. Now I write down whoever shouldn't get scared first.

items.sourceNote: 英文 adulting meme「Tupperware fighting for territory in your cabinet」；改寫成保鮮盒與蓋子永遠配不成一對的比喻，本檔僅在購物車清單提過保鮮盒，沒有這個主題

zh-tw.content:
我家有一個抽屜，專門放保鮮盒。

裡面有十四個盒子、十一個蓋子。理論上只有三個盒子會沒有伴，實際上是——每次我手上拿的那個盒子，蓋子永遠不在。

我會蹲在那裡試第四個、第五個，最後拿一個大兩號的蓋子壓上去，卡不緊，撕一段膠帶貼住，塞進冰箱。

成年人的生活大概就是這個形狀：東西都在，就是配不起來。時間有、錢有、朋友也有，只是很少同時出現在同一天。

但飯還是要收好。所以我們就用膠帶。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次開廚房抽屜都要跟蓋子搏鬥的室友或另一半
variations: 我不缺蓋子，我缺的是剛好對得起來的那一個。
大人的難處不是東西不夠，是東西湊不成一套。

en.content:
There's one drawer in my kitchen for food containers.

Fourteen containers. Eleven lids. In theory that means three go without. In practice it means the lid for whichever container I'm holding is never in there.

So I crouch there trying a fourth one, a fifth one, then jam on a lid two sizes too big, tape down one corner, and shove it in the fridge.

That's roughly the shape of adult life: everything's there, none of it matches. Time exists, money exists, friends exist — they just rarely show up on the same day.

The leftovers still need saving though. So we use tape.
en.editorNote: For the roommate or partner who fights that drawer every single night
variations: I'm not short on lids. I'm short on the one that actually fits.
The adult problem isn't not having enough. It's having enough of everything and none of it in a set.

items.sourceNote: 英文 adulting meme「Have you ever cooked spaghetti and thought, this is exactly the right amount?」；改寫成一個人住抓不準份量、媽媽的手感是失敗換來的，本檔沒有份量主題

zh-tw.content:
一個人住那麼久了，我到現在還是抓不準份量。

想煮一人份的麵，抓一把，覺得看起來太可憐，再加一點——煮出來剛好夠三個成年男生吃。

於是中午吃、晚上吃，隔天早上打開冰箱，那盒麵還在那裡看著我。它已經不是食物了，它是我的功課。

小時候媽媽煮的份量永遠剛剛好，我一直以為那是天分。後來才知道那不是天分，是煮了二十年、煮壞過幾百次留下來的手感。

所以我沒有很沮喪。我只是還在第三年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個冰箱裡永遠有一盒昨天煮太多的朋友
variations: 我不是煮太多，我是很有信心地為一個不存在的家庭煮飯。
媽媽的「剛剛好」不是天分，是幾百次煮太多換來的。

en.content:
Years of living alone and I still can't judge a portion.

I go to make pasta for one, grab a handful, decide it looks sad, add a little more — and produce enough to feed three grown men.

So I eat it for lunch. Then dinner. Then I open the fridge the next morning and the container is still looking at me. It stopped being food a while ago. It's homework now.

My mom's portions were always exactly right and I assumed that was a talent. It wasn't. It was twenty years of cooking and a few hundred times of getting it wrong.

So I'm not discouraged. I'm just on year three.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose fridge always holds one container of yesterday's overshoot
variations: I don't cook too much. I cook confidently for a family that does not exist.
Mom's "just right" was never a gift. It was a few hundred nights of way too much.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常見「咖啡因不再免費」的梗；改寫成下午兩點後的咖啡禁令與「為幾小時後的自己著想」的角度，本檔沒有咖啡因時效主題

zh-tw.content:
二十二歲的時候，咖啡是燃料。晚上十點喝一杯，通宵，隔天照常上班，中午還吃得下兩碗飯。

現在咖啡有時效。過了下午兩點就不能碰，碰了，凌晨兩點的我會躺在床上，眼睛睜得很大，腦袋清醒得像剛開機。

所以我學會了看時間喝咖啡。不是我變養生，是我已經很清楚代價由誰付——是凌晨那個我，而他今天沒有做錯任何事。

長大就是這樣：你開始替好幾個小時以後的自己著想，因為你們見過面了，你知道他有多累。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個下午三點還在點大杯拿鐵的同事，順便附上一句保重
variations: 以前咖啡是提神用的，現在咖啡是要還的。
我喝咖啡開始看時鐘，那大概就是對凌晨三點的自己負責的意思。

en.content:
At twenty-two, coffee was fuel. A cup at ten at night, straight through till morning, work the next day, full lunch.

Now coffee has a cutoff. Nothing after two in the afternoon, because if I slip, the version of me lying in bed at two in the morning is wide awake with a brain that just finished booting up.

So I watch the clock. Not because I got healthy — because I know exactly who pays for it. It's the 3 a.m. guy, and he didn't do anything wrong today.

That's growing up: you start looking out for a version of yourself a few hours away, because the two of you have met, and you know how tired he is.
en.editorNote: For the coworker still ordering a large latte at three in the afternoon
variations: Coffee used to be a boost. Now it's a loan.
I check the clock before I drink coffee. That's what being accountable to 3 a.m. me looks like.

items.sourceNote: 懷舊型 adulting memes 常提到「小時候的暑假很長」；改寫成八月驚覺一年過掉三分之二、大腦用新事件記時間的角度，本檔沒有時間感加速主題

zh-tw.content:
八月了。

我還在用「今年」這個詞規劃事情的時候，它已經過掉三分之二了。

小時候一個暑假可以長到讓人無聊。現在一年像一個很長的星期：禮拜一還在報稅，禮拜三就中秋了。

後來我看到一種說法——大腦是靠「新的事」在記時間的。小時候每天都有沒看過的東西，所以存下來的檔案很多，回頭看就很厚。長大以後每天都差不多，大腦沒東西可以存，就整段跳過去。

所以我最近開始故意走不一樣的路回家。不是想活得多精采，只是想讓今年再厚一點點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在月初或年中，那種突然驚覺時間不見了的時候發
variations: 一年過得快不是因為時間變快，是因為大腦覺得沒什麼好記的。
我開始走不一樣的路回家，只是為了讓今年看起來厚一點。

en.content:
It's August.

I'm still saying "this year" like I'm planning something, and two-thirds of it is already gone.

One summer break used to be long enough to get bored in. Now a year feels like one long week: Monday I'm doing my taxes, Wednesday it's mid-autumn.

Then I read an explanation for it. The brain keeps time with new things. As a kid every day had something you'd never seen, so the files piled up, and looking back it felt thick. As an adult the days match each other, the brain has nothing worth saving, and it skips the whole stretch.

So lately I've been walking home a different way on purpose. Not to live some remarkable life. Just to make this year a little thicker.
en.editorNote: For the start of a month, or that moment mid-year when you realize where the time went
variations: A year doesn't go fast because time sped up. It goes fast because your brain found nothing worth filing.
I take a different route home now, purely to give this year a few more pages.

items.sourceNote: adulting quote 合集常見「大人的快樂變得很便宜」主題；改寫成換床單的拖延與躺上去那三十秒，本檔無床單／寢具主題

zh-tw.content:
換床單這件事，從頭做到完大概十五分鐘。

我可以拖一個禮拜。

不是因為懶。是因為那一個禮拜裡，每一件事都是為了別人做的——為了工作、為了進度、為了不讓誰失望。輪到自己的時候，剩下的力氣只夠躺著。

然後某個晚上你突然把它換了。被套抖三次才對齊，枕頭套永遠塞歪一邊，你邊弄邊覺得自己很蠢。

可是躺上去的那三十秒，是真的很好。

長大以後很多快樂都變得很貴，這個沒有。它只要十五分鐘，跟一個你願意花在自己身上的晚上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合週末深夜發，或傳給那個床單已經三個禮拜沒換的自己
variations: 大人的奢侈品清單第一名：剛換好的床單，加上隔天不用早起。
十五分鐘的事我拖了一個禮拜，因為那一個禮拜我沒有一件事是為自己做的。

en.content:
Changing the sheets takes about fifteen minutes, start to finish.

I can put it off for a week.

Not because I'm lazy. Because for that whole week, everything I did was for someone else — for work, for a deadline, for not letting anyone down. By the time it's my turn, I have exactly enough left to lie down.

Then one night you just do it. The duvet cover takes three shakes to line up, the pillowcase ends up crooked no matter what, and you feel a little ridiculous the entire time.

But those first thirty seconds lying down are genuinely great.

Most joy gets expensive as you get older. This one didn't. It costs fifteen minutes and one evening you were willing to spend on yourself.
en.editorNote: For a late weekend night, or for the version of you whose sheets haven't been changed in three weeks
variations: Top of the adult luxury list: fresh sheets, and nowhere to be in the morning.
A fifteen-minute job took me a week, because that week had nothing in it that was for me.

items.sourceNote: adulting 語錄常提到回家前的沉默時刻；改寫成停好車後多坐五分鐘的身分切換「走廊」，本檔無此主題

zh-tw.content:
車停好了，鑰匙拔了，樓上的燈都看得到了。

然後你在駕駛座上又坐了五分鐘。

沒有在滑手機，歌也早就播完了。你只是還沒準備好推開那扇門，因為門的另一邊有人要叫你、有事要問你、有一疊你今天還沒處理的東西。

那五分鐘裡你誰都不是。不是誰的員工、不是誰的爸媽、不是那個什麼都會處理的人。就是一個坐著的人。

後來我不再覺得這是在逃避了。

房子跟房子之間需要走廊，一個人的兩種身分之間也需要。那五分鐘就是我的走廊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每天到家都要先在車上或樓下坐一下的人，告訴他這很正常
variations: 到家跟進門之間，我需要一個五分鐘的緩衝區。
那五分鐘我不是任何人的誰，這是我一天裡唯一的空白。

en.content:
Car's parked. Keys are out. You can see the lights on upstairs.

And you sit in the driver's seat for five more minutes.

Not on your phone. The song ended a while ago. You just aren't ready to push that door open, because on the other side of it someone will say your name, someone will ask you something, and there's a stack of things you didn't get to today.

For those five minutes you're nobody. Not an employee, not somebody's parent, not the person who handles everything. Just a person sitting down.

I stopped calling it avoidance.

Rooms need hallways between them. So do a person's two roles. Those five minutes are my hallway.
en.editorNote: For anyone who sits in the car a minute before walking inside — it's normal
variations: I need a five-minute buffer between arriving home and being home.
For those five minutes I'm not anyone's anything. It's the only blank space in my day.

items.sourceNote: adulting memes 常笑「大人的包包裡什麼都有」；改寫成隨身物品是被生活教出來的、而且多半不是給自己用的，本檔無隨身包主題

zh-tw.content:
我十九歲出門，口袋裡是手機、鑰匙、一張悠遊卡，就這樣。

現在我的包裡有：胃藥、OK 繃、一小包面紙、行動電源、備用的線、一支原子筆，還有一顆不知道放多久的喉糖。

年輕的時候，我覺得會帶這些東西的人很囉唆。

後來才知道那不是囉唆，是被教過。你在捷運上胃痛過一次，就會開始帶胃藥；你看過朋友的小孩在餐廳跌倒流血，就會開始帶 OK 繃。

而且很妙——這些東西幾乎都不是給自己用的。

包包重了兩百公克，換到的是「有人需要的時候我拿得出來」。這大概就是長大最不浪漫、也最實在的那一面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個包包永遠像百寶袋、每次都剛好拿得出你需要的東西的朋友
variations: 會隨身帶 OK 繃的人，通常都被生活教過一次。
包包變重不是因為東西變多，是因為要照顧的人變多了。

en.content:
At nineteen I left the house with a phone, keys, and a transit card. That was it.

Now my bag holds stomach medicine, band-aids, a travel pack of tissues, a power bank, a spare cable, a pen, and one cough drop of unknown age.

I used to think people who carried all that were fussy.

They're not fussy. They've been taught. You get a stomachache on the train once and you start carrying the medicine. You watch a friend's kid scrape a knee at a restaurant and you start carrying band-aids.

And here's the strange part — almost none of it is for me.

The bag got half a pound heavier, and what I got back is being the person who can produce the thing when somebody needs it. That's the least romantic and most real part of growing up.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose bag is a whole supply closet and always has what you need
variations: Anyone who carries band-aids got taught by something.
My bag didn't get heavier because I own more. It got heavier because more people count on me.

items.sourceNote: adulting quote 合集常寫大人的消費觀；改寫成把時間成本算進價格，刻意區別於本檔既有的超市比單價／湊免運兩則

zh-tw.content:
二十幾歲買東西只問一句：多少錢。

現在我會問：可以用幾年、壞了找誰、耗材多少、保固幾個月、不能修的話丟掉麻不麻煩。

店員大概覺得我很難搞。

但我不是變摳。我是算過了——便宜的那一台會在第十一個月壞掉，然後我要請半天假在家等人來看，要打三通電話問到底誰負責，要重新研究一次一模一樣的規格，最後再花一次錢。

那個下午值多少，只有付過的人知道。

長大就是你開始把時間跟心力一起放進價格裡算。標籤上那個數字，從來都不是全部。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在購物網站上開三十個分頁比規格、遲遲不敢按結帳的朋友
variations: 真正的價格是標價，加上它壞掉那天你要賠進去的那個下午。
我不是變摳，我是被便宜貨好好教過一次。

en.content:
In my twenties, buying something meant one question: how much.

Now I ask how many years it lasts, who fixes it, what the refills cost, how long the warranty runs, and how much of a hassle it is to throw out if nobody can repair it.

The salesperson probably thinks I'm a nightmare.

But I'm not cheap. I've done the math. The cheap one dies in month eleven, and then I take a half day off to wait for a repair guy, make three calls to find out whose problem it is, research the exact same specs all over again, and pay for it a second time.

Only the people who've spent that afternoon know what it was worth.

Growing up is when you start putting your time and your patience into the price. The number on the tag was never the whole number.
en.editorNote: For the friend with thirty comparison tabs open who still hasn't hit checkout
variations: The real price is the sticker plus the afternoon you'll lose the day it breaks.
I'm not cheap. I just got taught once, by something cheap.

items.sourceNote: 月老參拜流程與供品（喜糖、鉛錢、紅線、夾鏈袋）細節查證自參拜指南；內容原創，寫成大人願望清單的改變，本檔尚無七夕／月老題材

zh-tw.content:
七夕還有十天，月老廟前面已經在排隊了。

我是陪朋友去的。櫃台那份供品裡有喜糖、鉛錢，還有一條紅線，用夾鏈袋裝好，怕你弄丟。排在我前面的都是看起來很會處理事情的大人，一個手上還提著電腦包，剛剛才在騎樓講完一通工作電話。

二十五歲的時候，我求的是「讓我遇到一個很愛我的人」。

今天輪到我站到前面，我在心裡講的是：作息正常、碗會自己洗掉、吵架願意把話講完。

後來我才知道，七夕本來不是情人節，是乞巧，是求手藝的日子。我大概從第一年就拜錯重點了。

不過把日子過好，其實也是一種手藝。這樣算起來，說不定我一直都拜對了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個拉你在七夕前先去月老廟排隊、還一直強調「我只是陪你」的朋友
variations: 大人的姻緣願望清單，第一項不是心動，是作息正常。
我不再求一個很愛我的人，我求一個吵架願意把話講完的人。

en.content:
Ten days before Qixi, the matchmaker god's temple already has a line out to the street.

I came to keep a friend company. The offering set at the counter is candy, a lucky coin and a red thread, sealed in a little zip bag so you won't lose it. Everyone ahead of us looked extremely competent — laptop bags, one guy wrapping up a work call before he stepped inside.

At twenty-five I asked for someone who would love me a lot.

Today, standing at the front, what I said in my head was: keeps regular hours, washes their own dishes, stays in the room until an argument is actually finished.

I only found out later that Qixi was never a romance festival. It was a day for praying to be good with your hands. So I've been asking for the wrong thing since year one.

Then again, keeping a life running is a craft too. By that math, maybe I was on topic all along.
en.editorNote: For the friend who dragged you to the temple line and keeps insisting they're only there for you
variations: Grown-up love wishlist: nothing about butterflies, everything about a regular bedtime.
I stopped asking for someone who loves me hard. Now I ask for someone who finishes the conversation.

items.sourceNote: adulting 語錄常寫決策疲勞；改寫成剪頭髮只說「跟上次一樣」的具體場景，刻意區別於本檔既有的晚餐選擇疲勞一則

zh-tw.content:
我現在坐上那張椅子，只講五個字：跟上次一樣。

二十幾歲不是這樣的。那時候我三個月換一次髮型，手機裡存著照片，會認真跟設計師討論瀏海要落在哪裡，剪壞了也沒差，反正頭髮會長，日子也還很長。

現在我只想閉上眼睛四十分鐘。

不是我變得沒有想像力。是這個禮拜我已經決定過：那個案子要不要接、每天晚餐吃什麼、家裡壞掉的那台要修還是要換、要不要跟某個人把話說開。輪到頭髮的時候，我真的沒有了。

所以有一個地方，你坐下來什麼都不用重新解釋，對方就知道你要什麼——那不是一成不變，那是我這禮拜唯一一件不用動腦的事。

大人的安穩，很多時候就長這樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個設計師換了三間店、他也一路跟著換三間店的朋友
variations: 「跟上次一樣」這五個字，是一個很累的大人能交出去的最高信任。
我不是沒有想法，是我這禮拜的決定額度提早用完了。

en.content:
"Same as last time" is the entire conversation I have at the salon now.

In my twenties it went differently. New cut every three months, reference photos saved on my phone, a real discussion about where the bangs should land. A bad cut didn't matter — hair grows back, and there was a lot of time left.

Now I just want to close my eyes for forty minutes.

It isn't that I ran out of imagination. It's that this week I already decided whether to take the project, what's for dinner five nights running, whether the broken thing at home gets fixed or replaced, whether to finally have that conversation. By the time it's my hair's turn, there is nothing left in the tank.

So a place where you sit down and never have to explain yourself again isn't boring. It's the one thing all week that asks nothing of me.

A lot of grown-up peace looks exactly like that.
en.editorNote: For the friend who has followed the same stylist through three different salons
variations: "Same as last time" is the most trust a tired adult can hand anybody.
I have opinions. I just spent this week's decisions before I got to the chair.

items.sourceNote: adulting 圖文常見「大人的生日很安靜」；改寫成自己訂蛋糕＋深夜那則訊息，本檔尚無生日主題單則

zh-tw.content:
今年生日那天我在開會。

十一點多，群組裡有人貼了一張蛋糕貼圖，我回了一個謝謝。中午自己去買了那份想很久的便當，比平常貴七十塊，覺得非常值得。晚上的蛋糕是我自己訂的，六吋，因為切太大會吃不完。

小時候生日是一個被準備好的日子：有人幫你插蠟燭、關燈、假裝很驚喜。長大以後，它變成一個你要自己記得對自己好一點的日子。

那天十一點五十分，一個很久沒聯絡的朋友傳訊息進來：「差點忘記，還好趕上。」

沒有禮物，就一句話。我坐在沙發上看了很久。

長大以後最難得的不是有人幫你辦一場，是在一個大家都很忙的世界裡，還有人把你放在會想起來的位置上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每年都拖到晚上十一點五十分才敲你、但十年來一次都沒漏掉的朋友
variations: 大人的生日：蛋糕自己訂、蠟燭自己插、願望自己許，然後照常上班。
最好的生日禮物，是有人在最後十分鐘想起你。

en.content:
Birthdays as an adult: I spent mine in a meeting.

Around eleven someone dropped a cake sticker in the group chat and I typed thanks. At lunch I bought myself the expensive lunch box I'd been eyeing for weeks, worth every cent. The cake that night I ordered myself. Small size, because nobody was coming over to help me finish a big one.

As a kid, your birthday is a day other people prepare. Candles, lights off, everyone pretending to be surprised. Later it turns into a day you have to remember to be kind to yourself on.

Then at 11:50 p.m., a message from a friend I hadn't spoken to in a year: "Almost missed it. Made it."

No gift. One line. I sat on the couch and read it a few times.

The rare thing isn't being thrown a party. It's that in a world where everyone is busy, somebody still keeps you somewhere they walk past.
en.editorNote: For the friend who remembers your birthday every single year with ten minutes to spare
variations: Adult birthday: order your own cake, light your own candle, make your own wish, log on at nine.
Best gift available: somebody thinking of you at 11:50 p.m.

items.sourceNote: adulting 合集常寫大人什麼都自己扛；改寫成第一次開口求助的完整場景與後果，區別於本檔既有的「打電話很難」兩則

zh-tw.content:
上禮拜我終於把那句話講出來了：「這個我做不完，可以幫我一下嗎？」

我練習了兩天。真的，在腦中排演過三種說法，想過他會不會覺得我不行、會不會從此每件事都不太放心交給我。

結果同事說：「好啊，哪一段？」

五個字。然後那件事就解決了。

沒有人教過我們這個。小時候被稱讚的都是「你好乖，都不用人操心」，於是我們長成一種很會自己撐的大人：東西再重也自己搬，難過也等到沒人的時候。

後來我才慢慢懂，開口求助不是把自己變小，是把一個機會遞給對方——讓他也可以當那個幫得上忙的人。

那句話真的很難講。可是講完之後，天沒有塌下來，只是有人走過來，幫你把另外一頭抬起來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個凌晨兩點還在自己一個人趕整份簡報、你問他還好嗎只回「還好」的同事
variations: 求助不是把自己變小，是給對方一個當好人的機會。
成年人最難講的一句台詞：可以幫我一下嗎。

en.content:
"Can you help me with this?" took me two days to say out loud.

I rehearsed it. Three versions in my head, plus a full projection of how my coworker would decide I couldn't handle things, and how nothing important would ever come my way again.

What he actually said was: "Sure, which part?"

Three words. Then it was handled.

Nobody teaches us this one. The praise we grew up on was for being easy — no trouble, never needs anything — so we turned into adults who are very good at carrying things alone. Heavy box, carry it yourself. Bad day, wait until the room is empty.

It took me a long time to see that asking doesn't shrink you. It hands somebody else a chance to be the person who helped.

The sentence is still hard to say. But when you say it, the sky stays up. Someone just walks over and lifts the other end.
en.editorNote: For the coworker still building the whole deck at 2 a.m. who answers "all good" every time you check in
variations: Asking for help doesn't shrink you. It gives someone else a chance to be useful.
Hardest line in the adult script: can you help me with this.

items.sourceNote: 2026 行事曆話題：八月整個月沒有國定假日、特休要怎麼排；改寫成自己在月曆上畫一個紅圈的原創場景，本檔無月曆／國定假日主題（特休只在 aq-311 的變化句出現過）

zh-tw.content:
翻到八月那一頁，整個月沒有一天是紅的。

小時候我根本不看月曆，因為八月整個月都是我的，哪天紅哪天黑一點都不重要。現在我會把日曆拉開，很認真地算：這個月有幾個週末、哪一天請一天可以變成四天、哪一週的會最少。算完的結論是，三十一天全部都要上班，只是穿著夏天的外衣。

那天我拿紅筆，在下禮拜三的格子上自己畫了一個圈。

那天沒有節日，沒有人放假，也不會有人祝我什麼。我只是把它留下來了，什麼都不排，連要拿來做什麼都還沒想好——沒想好才是重點。

大人的紅字沒有人會發，只能自己畫一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在群組裡哀號「八月一天紅字都沒有」的同事，順便叫他自己排一天
variations: 小時候等紅字，長大後自己畫紅字。
沒有人會發假給大人，你只能自己圈一天下來，然後守住它。

en.content:
I flipped to August and there isn't one red day on the whole page.

As a kid I never checked. August belonged to me start to finish, so which days were holidays made no difference. Now I spread the calendar out and do math: how many weekends, which single day off would stretch into four, which week has the fewest meetings. Conclusion — thirty-one working days in a row, wearing a summer costume.

So I took a red pen and drew a circle around next Wednesday.

Nothing happens that day. Nobody gets off work, nobody will message me about it. I just claimed it. Nothing scheduled, and I haven't decided what it's for yet — not deciding is the whole point.

Nobody hands an adult a day off. You draw your own.
en.editorNote: For the group chat complaining that August has zero holidays — send it with "so book one yourself"
variations: As a kid you wait for the red days. As an adult you draw them.
Nobody gives adults a holiday. You circle one and then defend it.

items.sourceNote: adulting 討論常見「開始照顧父母」的轉折點；改寫成診間座位與醫生視線的具體場景，刻意區別於本檔既有的健檢緊急聯絡人（aq-354）與家庭群組方向反轉（aq-340）

zh-tw.content:
上禮拜陪我爸回診。

進診間我本來要坐旁邊那張椅子，護理師說家屬坐後面就好，我就停在他肩膀後半步的位置。

醫生開始講的時候，我才發現他的眼睛是看著我的。血糖、藥要怎麼調、下次抽血前三天不能吃什麼——每一句都是對我講的，我爸坐在中間，安安靜靜地點頭。

那一刻我知道自己的位置換了。以前坐在後面聽、在後面記的人是我媽，我只要坐在中間就好。現在換我在後面，掏出手機把醫生的話一句一句打進備忘錄，還多問了一句「那要空腹幾個小時」。

回家的路上我爸說：他講太快了，我沒聽清楚。

我說沒關係，我記下來了。

這大概是我這輩子講過最像大人的一句話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個開始陪爸媽跑醫院、手機備忘錄裡存著長輩用藥的朋友
variations: 角色互換不是某一天突然發生的，是醫生開始對著你講話的那一刻。
以前是我媽坐在後面幫我記，現在換我坐在後面。

en.content:
Took my dad to his follow-up last week.

I went for the chair next to him, but the nurse said family sits behind, so I ended up half a step back from his shoulder.

When the doctor started talking, I realized he was looking at me. Blood sugar, how we're adjusting the dose, what he can't eat for three days before the next blood draw — every sentence aimed at me, while my dad sat in the middle nodding quietly.

That's when I noticed my seat had changed. My mom used to be the one behind, listening and remembering; all I had to do was sit in the middle. Now I'm the one in back, typing the doctor's words into my phone line by line, asking one extra question about how many hours of fasting.

On the drive home my dad said, he talked too fast, I didn't catch it.

I said don't worry, I wrote it down.

That is the most grown-up sentence I have ever said out loud.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose notes app now holds their parents' prescriptions
variations: The switch doesn't happen on a birthday. It happens the day the doctor starts looking at you.
My mom used to be the one taking notes. Now I'm the one in the back with the phone out.

items.sourceNote: adulting 推文常笑「大人看不完一部電影」；改寫成 118 分鐘分四個晚上、每次倒回十五分鐘的具體場景與「娛樂分期付款」的說法，本檔既有的睡眠題材寫的是失眠與熬夜代價，沒有這個角度

zh-tw.content:
片長一百一十八分鐘，我看了四個晚上。

不是沒時間。是每天洗完澡坐下來，片頭跑完，眼皮就先下班了。隔天再打開，還得往回拉十五分鐘，因為我完全不記得自己是在哪裡斷線的。

第四個晚上終於看到片尾，然後發現中間有一整段我根本沒看過。兇手是誰我到現在還是用猜的，而且我猜得很有信心。

二十歲的時候，我可以在戲院連看兩場，散場還去吃宵夜。

現在我的娛樂是分期付款的：一集影集分兩天、一本書一次三頁、一部電影四個晚上。

其實也沒有很難過。慢慢看完的東西，好像在腦袋裡留得比較久——雖然留下來的那幾段，多半不是導演最想給我的那幾段。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個片單存了兩百部、每一部都停在前二十分鐘的朋友
variations: 大人的娛樂是分期付款的：一部電影四個晚上，結局還是用猜的。
我不是看不完電影，我只是每天晚上都提早退場。

en.content:
Runtime: 118 minutes. It took me four nights.

Not a time problem. I sit down after my shower, the opening credits roll, and my eyelids clock out. Next night I have to scrub back fifteen minutes, because I have no idea where I dropped off.

On night four I finally reached the credits and discovered there was a whole stretch in the middle I never actually watched. I still don't know who did it. I have a theory, and I'm confident about it.

At twenty I could sit through a double feature and go out for food afterward.

Now my entertainment arrives in installments: one episode across two nights, three pages of a book, one movie over four evenings.

Honestly, not the worst arrangement. The things I take slowly seem to stay with me longer — though the parts that stayed are probably not the parts the director was aiming for.
en.editorNote: For the friend with 200 films in their watchlist, every one of them stopped at minute twenty
variations: Adult movie night: one film, four evenings, and the ending is still a guess.
I don't fail to finish movies. I just leave early, every single night.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8/7–8/13 分區實施的城鎮韌性（防空）演習為時事背景；內容原創，寫成超市裡一群大人安靜等解除的場景，本檔無演習／警報主題（既有的「警報」只出現在垃圾車音樂與颱風兩則）

zh-tw.content:
警報響的時候，我正在超市挑蛋。

廣播說演習期間請留在室內，於是一整間店的陌生人就停在原地。有人低頭滑手機，有人壓低聲音講電話說「我大概晚二十分鐘到」，一位阿姨把籃子放在地上，順手把香蕉一根一根挑好。沒有人慌，也沒有人閒聊，大家只是安安靜靜地站著，等它結束。

小時候的演習，是躲在桌子底下憋笑，因為那半小時不用上課。

現在的演習，是被硬塞進一天裡的三十分鐘空白。而我站在冷藏櫃前，腦中冒出的第一個念頭是：出門前冷氣好像沒關。

解除的廣播一響，全場的人幾乎同時動了起來，推著車繼續往前，好像剛剛什麼都沒發生過。

大人連被迫停下來的時候，想起的都還是那些還沒做完的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 演習日或警報解除後轉發，附一句：那三十分鐘你腦袋裡在想什麼？
variations: 小時候的演習是不用上課的三十分鐘，現在的演習是還沒做完的三十分鐘。
被迫站著不動半小時，我想的第一件事竟然是家裡冷氣有沒有關。

en.content:
The siren went off while I was picking out eggs.

The announcement said stay indoors for the duration of the drill, so a supermarket full of strangers simply stopped where they stood. One guy scrolling. One woman dropping her voice to say I'll be about twenty minutes late. An older lady set her basket on the floor and went through the bananas one at a time. Nobody panicked. Nobody chatted. We all just stood there quietly, waiting for it to end.

As a kid, a drill meant crouching under a desk trying not to laugh, because that was thirty minutes of no class.

Now a drill is thirty blank minutes wedged into the day. And standing in front of the refrigerated case, the first thought in my head was: I think I left the AC on.

When the all-clear came, the whole store started moving at once, carts rolling forward like nothing had happened.

Even when an adult is forced to stand still, the first thing we reach for is whatever we haven't finished.
en.editorNote: Send on a drill day, with: so what was actually in your head for those thirty minutes?
variations: A drill used to be thirty minutes off school. Now it's thirty minutes I still owe someone.
Made to stand still for half an hour, and my first thought was whether I left the AC running.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年台灣外食漲價、都會區便當普遍破百的新聞為時事背景；內容原創，寫成自助餐保溫檯前的心算與「飯少一點」的細節，本檔既有便當相關只談冷凍庫存糧與家常菜，無外食物價主題

zh-tw.content:
自助餐夾三樣，一百三。

我沒說什麼，刷了卡就走。走出店門才開始在腦袋裡跑那串算術：一個月上班二十二天，午餐一天一百三，就是兩千八百六。再加上早餐、加上下午偶爾想喝的那一杯，一個月光是吃掉的數字，差不多是我十年前一整個月的房租。

以前我挑店只看好不好吃。現在我進門會先掃一眼保溫檯，心裡默默排順序：這格看起來紮實、這格是湊數的、這格夾下去一定很貴。夾菜的手變得很有計畫，像在玩一個不能存檔的遊戲。

前面那位阿姨只夾了兩樣，跟老闆說：「飯少一點。」老闆點點頭，多舀了一瓢湯給她。

我後來也學會了。不是為了省那幾十塊，是想在什麼都變貴的日子裡，替自己留一點還做得了主的感覺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天中午站在店門口猶豫三分鐘的同事，配一句：你今天那餐多少？
variations: 以前挑店看好不好吃，現在先掃一眼保溫檯，心裡默默排哪一格划算。
一百三的午餐，附贈一整套腦內算術。

en.content:
Three items at the cafeteria counter. Four dollars twenty.

I didn't say anything. I tapped my card and left. It was outside on the sidewalk that the arithmetic started running: twenty-two workdays a month, lunch at four twenty, that's ninety-two something. Add breakfast. Add the afternoon coffee I sometimes want. What I spend in a month on just eating is roughly what a month of rent cost me ten years ago.

I used to pick a place based on whether the food was good. Now I scan the steam table on the way in and quietly rank it: that tray looks substantial, that one's filler, that one will cost me. My tongs have a strategy now. It's like playing a game with no save file.
