The woman ahead of me took only two things and asked for less rice. The guy behind the counter nodded and ladled her extra soup.

I've started doing the same. Not to save the change. Just to keep some small say in things, in a year where everything got more expensive without asking me.
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who spends three minutes frozen outside the lunch place every day
variations: I used to pick lunch by taste. Now I scan the counter and rank it by value.
A four-dollar lunch, served with a full round of mental math.

items.sourceNote: 物價與消費心態討論串為靈感；內容原創，寫成修鞋、縫扣子、鎖桌腳的修補心態，本檔無「修理／保固／針線」相關題材（既有的修東西都是打電話叫爸或叫師傅）

zh-tw.content:
我把一雙鞋拿去換底，三百五。

同一款新的在架上賣一千八。二十五歲的我會直接買新的，反正舊的也穿兩年了，換一雙比較快。三十幾歲的我站在攤子前面，看老闆拿刀把舊底一層一層削掉，覺得三百五換回一雙已經合腳的鞋，非常划算。

不知道從哪一年開始，我變成那種買東西會先問保固幾年的人。襯衫掉了扣子，我會翻出針線盒縫回去，縫得歪歪的，反正穿在裡面沒人看得到。桌腳鬆了，我不換桌子，我找螺絲起子。

不是變窮，也不是變小氣。是我終於知道，一樣東西願意留在你身邊很久，其實不容易——它撐過了兩次搬家、撐過了那幾個心情很差的月份，現在還在。

換新的很快。修好的比較久。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個桌上放著針線盒、抽屜裡收著一整袋螺絲的朋友
variations: 換新的很快，修好的比較久。
三百五換回一雙已經合腳的鞋，我覺得非常划算。

en.content:
I got a pair of shoes resoled. Eleven dollars.

The same shoe, new, is sixty on the shelf. At twenty-five I'd have just bought the new pair — the old ones had two years on them, replacing is faster. At thirty-something I stood at the counter watching the guy shave the old sole off in layers, thinking eleven dollars to get back a pair already broken in is a bargain.

Somewhere along the way I turned into a person who asks how long the warranty is before buying. When a shirt loses a button I dig out the sewing kit and put it back on crooked, because nobody sees the inside of a shirt. When a table leg goes wobbly I don't replace the table. I find the screwdriver.

It isn't about being broke, or being cheap. It's that I finally understand how rare it is for a thing to stay with you a long time. It survived two moves. It survived those few bad months. It's still here.

Buying new is fast. Fixing lasts longer.
en.editorNote: For the friend with a sewing kit on the desk and a bag of spare screws in the drawer
variations: Buying new is fast. Fixing lasts longer.
Eleven dollars to get back a pair of shoes already broken in — best deal of my month.

items.sourceNote: 體力衰退與日常運動缺口的普遍討論為背景；內容原創，寫成電梯維修三天爬五樓的身體變化，本檔既有身體題材集中在落枕、腰痛、熬夜，無樓梯／體能回升角度

zh-tw.content:
電梯上貼了一張紙：維修中，預計三天。

我住五樓。第一趟提著兩袋東西上去，爬到三樓半的時候，我停在轉角假裝在看手機。其實我是在等心跳慢下來，順便讓後面那位先過。

十八歲的時候，我可以一次跨兩階衝到頂樓，只為了拿一個忘記帶的東西，下來的時候還在跳。那時候我不知道爬樓梯需要力氣，因為它從來不需要。

第三天下午，我提著晚餐爬到四樓，忽然發現自己一次都沒停。不是突然變年輕，是身體在三天之內默默把自己調回來了一點。

原來它一直都還願意進步，只是這幾年我從來沒給過它機會。

電梯修好那天，我還是按了按鈕。但有一件事跟以前不一樣了：我知道那五層樓，我爬得上去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個說「等有空再開始運動」的人，配一句：從你家那幾層樓開始就好
variations: 不是身體壞了，是這幾年我從來沒給過它機會。
電梯修好那天我還是按了按鈕，但我知道那五層樓我爬得上去。

en.content:
A sign went up on the elevator: out of service, three days.

I live on the fifth floor. First trip up with two bags of groceries, I stopped on the landing between three and four and pretended to check my phone. I was actually waiting for my heart rate to come down, and letting the guy behind me pass.

At eighteen I could take those stairs two at a time to the roof just to grab something I'd forgotten, and still be bouncing on the way down. I didn't know climbing stairs took anything out of you, because it never had.

Third day, carrying dinner up, I got to the fourth floor and realized I hadn't stopped once. Not because I'd gotten younger. Because in three days my body had quietly recalibrated.

Turns out it was always willing to improve. I just hadn't given it a single chance in years.

The day the elevator came back, I pressed the button anyway. But something is different now: I know I can climb those five floors.
en.editorNote: For the person who keeps saying they'll start working out when things calm down
variations: My body wasn't broken. I just hadn't given it a chance in years.
I still press the elevator button. I just know now that I don't have to.

items.sourceNote: 世代與年齡定義的社群討論為靈感；內容原創，寫成回老家過夜、舊房間變成堆放區的場景，本檔既有回老家題材只寫過年桌次與角色降級，無「舊房間被日子填滿」角度

zh-tw.content:
回家住一晚，推開我以前那間房，先聞到的是紙箱的味道。

床還在，但床上疊著兩箱過年用的東西。書桌變成放藥的地方，抽屜裡我小學的獎狀跟我媽的血壓計很和平地擺在一起。牆上那張海報也還在，只是邊邊已經捲起來了。

我媽從我後面探頭進來：「東西我先堆一下而已，你要住我馬上收。」

她說「馬上收」的時候，語氣有點抱歉。可是那間房空了十年，她只是慢慢地把日子搬了進去，這很合理。

我說不用收，我睡客廳沙發就好。半夜起來倒水，經過那扇門，我才想通一件事：

那不是我的房間被佔走了，是這個家沒有停在我離開的那一年，它自己繼續過下去了。而我真正的家，現在是另一間要自己繳水電費的房子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回老家過夜的那個晚上發，配一句：你以前那間房，現在放什麼？
variations: 那間房空了十年，我媽只是慢慢地把日子搬了進去。
不是我的房間被佔走了，是這個家沒有停在我離開的那一年。

en.content:
I stayed at my parents' place overnight. Opened the door to my old room and the first thing I smelled was cardboard.

The bed is still there, with two boxes of holiday decorations stacked on it. The desk is where the medicine lives now, and in the drawer my elementary school certificates sit peacefully next to my mom's blood pressure cuff. The poster is still on the wall. The corners have curled.

My mom leaned in behind me. "I just put a few things in here. If you're sleeping over I'll clear it out right now."

She said "right now" a little apologetically. But that room sat empty for ten years, and she'd simply been moving daily life into it. That's reasonable.

I told her not to bother, I'd take the couch. Getting up at 2 a.m. for water, passing that door, I finally understood something:

My room wasn't taken from me. This house just didn't stop at the year I left — it kept living. And my actual home is now a different place, one where I pay the utilities myself.
en.editorNote: Post it on the night you sleep over at your parents' house: so what's in your old bedroom now?
variations: That room sat empty for ten years. She was just moving life into it.
My room wasn't taken from me. The house simply didn't stop at the year I left.

items.sourceNote: 肩頸痠痛與按摩的討論為靈感；內容原創，寫成「按摩從犒賞變成回廠保養」的場景，本檔既有身體題材集中在健檢、看牙與吃保健食品，無按摩／推拿角度

zh-tw.content:
二十五歲去按摩，是犒賞自己。三十五歲去按摩，是回廠。

躺下去五秒，師傅按到右邊肩胛骨那一塊，我整個人從床上彈起來。他很平靜地問：「你是不是每天打電腦超過八小時？」我說對。他又壓了一下：「而且滑鼠在右手，螢幕偏左邊。」

我趴在那裡，被一個第一次見面的人從背上讀出我整個工作型態，比我的年度考核還準。

結束的時候他說：「這個要固定來喔。」

以前聽到「固定來」我會覺得是推銷。現在我點開手機，把下個月的同一天先排進去了。

身體開始有固定要保養的地方，這件事不會有人發通知給你，是它自己找上門的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合按完走出店門、還在痠的時候發，配一句：你身體最先壞掉的是哪一塊？
variations: 以前按摩是犒賞，現在按摩是回廠。
師傅壓三下就講出我的工作型態，比年度考核還準。

en.content:
Booked a massage. Not as a treat this time — as maintenance.

Five seconds in, he found one spot under my right shoulder blade and I came off the table. He asked, completely calm: "Eight hours a day at a computer?" Yes. He pressed again. "Mouse on the right. Monitor sits off to your left."

Face down on that table, a stranger read my entire job off my back. More accurate than my performance review.

On the way out he said, "You should come regularly."

A few years ago that would have sounded like a sales pitch. Instead I opened my phone and booked the same day next month.

Your body starts having a standing maintenance appointment. Nobody sends you a notice about it. It just turns up.
en.editorNote: Post it walking out of the massage place still sore: which part of your body broke down first?
variations: A massage used to be a reward. Now it's scheduled maintenance.
Three presses and a stranger read my whole job off my back.

items.sourceNote: 預售屋與樣品屋參觀的討論為靈感；內容原創，寫成「沒有要買也去看」的週末場景，本檔既有題材只提過買房是成就感清單的一項，無看房／樣品屋角度，且刻意不寫房價數字與市場評論

zh-tw.content:
週末沒事，我們去看了預售屋。

沒有要買。我很清楚沒有要買，接待的人大概也看得出來，但他還是很認真地帶我們走完每一間。

樣品屋裡什麼都是好的：書櫃上擺著沒有人讀過的書，冰箱打開是空的，陽台的植物摸起來有一點塑膠。臥室的床我坐了一下，很硬，很乾淨，沒有人睡過。牆上掛著一張全家福，裡面那家人我不認識，笑得比我上一次拍照還開心。

出來以後太陽很兇，我們去對面買了兩杯飲料，坐在騎樓底下各自按計算機。按完誰都沒說話，然後我朋友說：「回去吧，我家冷氣比較涼。」

那天我才想通，我們不是去看房子的。我們是走進別人示範好的人生裡站了二十分鐘，然後回到自己那間有點亂、但每一樣東西都是自己買的房子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看完房回到家、把冷氣打開那一刻發，配一句：你上次站在樣品屋裡在想什麼？
variations: 樣品屋的冰箱打開是空的，牆上那家人笑得比我上次拍照還開心。
我們不是去看房子，是去別人示範好的人生裡站了二十分鐘。

en.content:
Toured a presale apartment on Saturday. Not buying. Just looking.

The agent could tell. He walked us through every room anyway.

Everything in a model unit is perfect: books on the shelf nobody has opened, a fridge that opens onto nothing, balcony plants that feel faintly like plastic. I sat on the bed. Firm, clean, never slept in. There was a family portrait on the wall. I don't know those people. They are smiling harder than I did in my last photo.

Outside it was too hot to stand in. We bought two drinks, sat under an awning, and each did the math on our phones. Nobody said anything for a while. Then my friend said, "Let's go, my AC is better."

That's when it landed. We hadn't gone to look at an apartment. We'd stood inside someone's demo version of a life for twenty minutes, then went home to our own place — messier, but every single thing in it we bought ourselves.
en.editorNote: Post it the moment you get home and turn your own AC on: what were you actually thinking inside that model unit?
variations: The model-unit fridge opens onto nothing, and the family on the wall smiles harder than I do.
Twenty minutes inside someone's demo version of a life, then back to my own.

items.sourceNote: 「白髮到底能不能拔」的醫療科普討論為靈感；內容原創，寫成早上照鏡子發現第一根白髮、想起小時候幫媽媽找白髮的場景，本檔既有頭髮題材只有髮廊「跟上次一樣」，無白髮角度；不寫任何醫療建議

zh-tw.content:
早上洗完臉抬起頭，右邊鬢角有一根白的。

手已經伸過去了，捏住，然後放開。

因為我突然想起小時候，我媽會坐在沙發上把頭低下來，叫我幫她找白頭髮，一根五塊。我拿著鑷子在她頭頂上翻得很認真，那時候覺得白頭髮是很遠很遠的東西，遠到跟我一點關係都沒有。

我在鏡子前面站了一下，決定留著它。

不是我看得多開。是我算過了：這種東西處理掉還會再有，而且現在也沒有人會坐在我旁邊，一根五塊地幫我找。

所以那根我留著了。它不是在提醒我幾歲，它是在提醒我，我媽當年也是這樣一個人站在鏡子前面，看完，然後若無其事地去上班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合早上發現第一根白髮的那天發，配一句：你的第一根白頭髮，留著還是處理掉了？
variations: 手已經伸過去了，捏住，又放開。
小時候幫我媽找白頭髮，一根五塊。那時候覺得那是很遠很遠的東西。

en.content:
One white hair, right temple. Spotted it this morning after washing my face.

My hand was already up there. Pinched it. Let go.

Because I suddenly remembered being a kid, my mom bending her head down on the couch, asking me to hunt through it for white hairs. Five bucks each. I'd go at the top of her head with tweezers, extremely serious about the job. Back then white hair was a far-off thing. Far enough that it had nothing to do with me.

I stood at the mirror for a second and decided to leave it there.

Not because I've made peace with anything. I just ran the numbers: deal with this one and there will be another, and nobody is going to sit down next to me and hunt for them at five bucks a piece.

So it stays. It isn't there to remind me how old I am. It's there to remind me that my mom once stood at a mirror exactly like this, looked, and then went to work like nothing had happened.
en.editorNote: Post it the morning you find your first white hair: did you keep it or deal with it?
variations: My hand was already up there. Pinched it. Let go.
Five bucks a white hair, hunting through my mom's head. It felt so far away then.

items.sourceNote: 警方居家安全守則中「就寢前關瓦斯總開關、門窗上鎖」的宣導為靈感；內容原創，寫成睡前固定巡一圈的習慣，以及發現這個順序是從父母那裡接手來的，本檔既有題材無「家裡最後一個睡的人」角度

zh-tw.content:
睡前我會在家裡走一圈。

瓦斯關了沒、後陽台那扇窗有沒有扣好、大門反鎖、廚房那盞燈。順序固定，全部走完不到兩分鐘，走完才睡得著。

前幾天我走到一半突然停住，因為我發現這個順序不是我自己想出來的。

小時候我房間的燈關掉以後，外面還會亮一陣子。然後有腳步聲從廚房走到陽台、再走回來，最後喀一聲，整間房子就暗了。那個聲音我聽了十幾年，從來沒有想過是誰在走，也沒有想過那個人為什麼永遠最後一個睡。

現在我住的地方只有我一個人。沒有人會聽到我的腳步聲，也沒有人在等那一聲喀。

但我還是每天走。有些習慣不是學來的，是你某一天接手的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合關掉家裡最後一盞燈的時候發，配一句：你家最後一個睡的人是誰？
variations: 瓦斯、陽台窗、大門反鎖、廚房那盞燈——順序固定，走完才睡得著。
有些習慣不是學來的，是你某一天接手的。

en.content:
Four things before bed, every night. Gas off. Back balcony window latched. Front door deadbolted. Kitchen light.

Same order every time. Under two minutes. I can't fall asleep until it's done.

The other night I stopped halfway through, because it hit me that I didn't come up with this order.

When I was a kid, the light outside my room stayed on a while after mine went off. Then footsteps, kitchen to balcony and back again, and finally one click, and the whole house went dark. I heard that for years. Never once wondered who was walking, or why that person was always the last one to bed.

I live alone now. Nobody hears my footsteps. Nobody is waiting on that click.

I still walk it every night. Some habits you don't learn. You take them over one day.
en.editorNote: Post it right after you kill the last light in the house: who's the last one to bed at your place?
variations: Gas, balcony window, deadbolt, kitchen light. Same order, every single night.
Some habits you don't learn. You take them over one day.

items.sourceNote: Mobile01「長大後才知道的事」討論串的網友共鳴為靈感；內容原創，寫成「沒有人發證書的成年技能清單」，本檔既有題材多為兩段對照式，缺少清單式盤點角度

zh-tw.content:
沒有人會發證書，可是你確實學會了這些事：

看一眼群組訊息，就知道這則不用回。
知道家裡退燒藥放在哪一格，也知道大概還剩幾顆。
牙醫說「這顆我們再觀察看看」，你聽得出來那句的意思是：開始存錢。
朋友傳來一句「最近還好嗎」，你分得出來那是問候，還是求救。
搬家報價聽兩家，就知道哪一家在灌水。

這些沒有考試，也沒有人幫你蓋章。你只是在一個又一個很普通的日子裡，把它們一件一件做完了，然後它們就是你的了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得自己一事無成的那天發，配一句：你身上有哪幾張沒人知道的證書？
variations: 牙醫說「這顆我們再觀察看看」，你聽得出來那句的意思是：開始存錢。
沒有考試，也沒有人蓋章。你就是會了。

en.content:
Nobody hands you a certificate, but you did learn all of this:

One glance at a group chat tells you this message doesn't need a reply.
You know which drawer the fever meds live in, and roughly how many are left.
When the dentist says "let's keep an eye on that one," you hear what it actually means: start saving.
When a friend texts "you doing okay?", you can tell whether that's small talk or a flare going up.
Two quotes from movers is enough to know which one is padding the number.

There's no exam for any of it, and nobody stamps your form. You just did these things one at a time, on very ordinary days, until they were yours.
en.editorNote: Post it on a day you feel like you've accomplished nothing: which certificates are you carrying that nobody knows about?
variations: "Let's keep an eye on that one" is dentist for: start saving.
No exam, no stamp. You just got good at it.

items.sourceNote: 大人學〈長大，是一種從慌亂到習慣的過程〉中「成年的日常由無名瑣事組成」的觀察為靈感；內容原創，改寫成朋友對話短劇，本檔既有題材無對白體

zh-tw.content:
「你最近在忙什麼？」

「就……忙啊。」

「忙什麼？」

「忙……」

我真的答不出來。不是不想講，是那些事沒有名字：比三家保養廠的價錢、追一筆退了兩次還沒進來的款、把家裡兩張約的到期日對起來、又幫我媽重設一次密碼。

「反正就是一些雜事。」我說。

「懂。」他說，「我也一樣。」

然後我們兩個就笑了。大人的忙大概都是這種忙：一整個禮拜過去，行事曆上乾乾淨淨什麼都沒有，人卻是空的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 被問「最近在忙什麼」卻卡住的時候發，配一句：你這禮拜忙的事，有名字嗎？
variations: 大人的忙，多半是沒有名字的忙。
一整個禮拜過去，行事曆上什麼都沒留下，人卻是空的。

en.content:
"So what have you been up to?"

"Just... busy."

"Busy with what?"

"Busy..."

And I had nothing. Not because I didn't want to answer — because none of it has a name. Getting three quotes on the car service. Chasing a refund that's failed twice. Lining up two renewal dates so they stop colliding. Resetting my mom's password. Again.

"Just stuff," I said.

"Yeah," he said. "Same."

And we both laughed. That's the adult kind of busy: a whole week goes by, the calendar stays completely empty, and you're running on fumes anyway.
en.editorNote: Post it when someone asks what you've been up to and you freeze: does anything you did this week have a name?
variations: Adult busy is mostly the kind of busy that has no name.
A whole week gone, nothing on the calendar, and you're still empty.

items.sourceNote: 食力〈8種常見調味料開封後實質保質期〉指出醬油開封後約一個月、辣椒醬約半年，包裝上的日期即失去參考價值；內容原創，寫成清冰箱時丟掉「跟自己搬過家的那罐醬」，本檔既有題材有保鮮盒但無清冰箱角度

zh-tw.content:
這禮拜終於把冰箱門那排瓶瓶罐罐清出來。

一罐辣椒醬，開過，剩三分之二。我把它翻過來看日期，整個人愣住——那是我上一個住處買的。也就是說，它跟我搬過一次家，坐過搬家公司的車，被我親手放進新冰箱，然後在門邊站到現在。

查了才知道，醬料只要開封，瓶身印的那個日期就不太算數了。醬油開了大概撐一個月，辣椒醬也就半年。我這罐早就不是食物，是紀念品。

丟。旁邊那罐從沒開過的沙拉醬，也丟。半罐硬掉的蜂蜜，一起。

冰箱門空出一整排。站在那裡看那排空位，才明白我丟掉的不是醬料，是我曾經以為自己會過的那種、會好好煮飯的生活。
zh-tw.editorNote: 清冰箱那天發，配一句：你冰箱門上最老的那罐，是什麼時候買的？
variations: 那罐辣椒醬跟我搬過一次家，坐過搬家公司的車，然後在冰箱門邊站到現在。
丟掉的不是醬料，是我以為自己會過的那種生活。

en.content:
Finally cleared out the row of jars in the fridge door this week.

One chili sauce, opened, two thirds left. I turned it over to check the date and just stopped — I bought that at my old place. Which means it moved apartments with me. It rode in the mover's truck. I put it into the new fridge with my own hands, and it has been standing in that door ever since.

Turns out that once a sauce is opened, the date printed on the jar stops meaning much. Soy sauce lasts about a month. Chili sauce maybe half a year. Mine hadn't been food for a long time. It was a souvenir.

Trash. The salad dressing next to it, never opened, also trash. Half a jar of honey gone solid, same trip.

The fridge door came out empty. Standing there looking at that empty row, I understood what I'd actually thrown away: not sauce, but the version of my life where I was going to cook properly.
en.editorNote: Post it on fridge-cleaning day: how old is the oldest jar in your fridge door?
variations: That chili sauce moved apartments with me. It rode in the mover's truck.
I wasn't throwing away sauce. I was throwing away the version of me who cooks.

items.sourceNote: 大人學〈關於如何成為大人這件事〉中「成熟不是不害怕，而是照樣行動」的論點為靈感；內容原創，壓縮成單句金句，與本檔多為長篇情境敘述形成節奏對比

zh-tw.content:
小時候覺得大人很勇敢。

長大才懂，大人只是把害怕排進行事曆——禮拜三看報告，禮拜五談加薪。怕歸怕，時間到了還是會去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在明知道會怕、但還是得去的前一晚發，配一句：你這禮拜排了哪一件會怕的事？
variations: 大人不是不怕，是把怕的事排進行事曆，時間到了照樣去。
勇敢不是心跳變慢，是行程沒有改。

en.content:
As a kid, adults looked brave.

Turns out adults just put the scary thing on the calendar — results on Wednesday, the raise conversation on Friday. Still scared. Still shows up.
en.editorNote: Post it the night before something you're dreading but going to anyway: what did you put on the calendar this week?
variations: Adults aren't unafraid. They just schedule the fear and show up on the day.
Brave isn't a slower heartbeat. It's an unchanged calendar.

items.sourceNote: Money101 白包奠儀指南（金額取單數、封面寫奠儀、袋口不封）為知識來源；內容原創，寫成第一次代表家裡包白包、在簿子上換成自己名字，本檔既有題材有紅包與喜帖，無白包角度

zh-tw.content:
上個月家裡有位長輩走了。以前遇到這種場合，我的工作就是跟著站、跟著鞠躬，紅包白包都是我爸在處理。

這次我媽在電話裡說：「你自己包一個。」

我查了很久才把規矩弄懂：金額要單數，不能包雙數，因為好事才成雙；封面寫「奠儀」；袋口不用封。這些沒有人正式教過我，可是每個大人好像都會。

到了現場，我把白包交到受賻處，在簿子上寫下自己的名字。寫的時候手有點抖。不是因為難過，是因為那一格以前寫的是我爸的名字。

後來我一直在想：所謂長大，大概就是有一天，簿子上那一格換成你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 第一次代表家裡出席喪禮之後發，配一句：你家的白包，現在是誰在包？
variations: 這些規矩沒有人正式教過我，可是每個大人好像都會。
所謂長大，大概就是有一天，簿子上那一格換成你的名字。

en.content:
We lost an elder in the family last month. At these things my job used to be simple: stand where I was told, bow when everyone bowed. My dad handled the envelopes, red ones and white ones alike.

This time my mom said it over the phone: "Prepare your own."

It took me a while to get the rules straight. The amount has to be an odd number, never even, because only good things come in pairs. You write the word for condolence money on the front. You leave the flap unsealed. Nobody ever formally taught me this, and yet every adult seems to know it.

At the hall I handed the envelope in and signed my name in the register. My hand shook a little. Not from grief. From the fact that the line used to have my father's name on it.

I keep coming back to it since. Growing up is maybe just this: one day the name in that register becomes yours.
en.editorNote: Post it after the first funeral you attended as the family's representative: who signs the register for your family now?
variations: Nobody formally taught me the rules, and yet every adult somehow knows them.
Growing up is maybe just this: one day the name in that register becomes yours.

items.sourceNote: 2026 中元普渡流程與租屋族簡易版說明；改寫為租屋族第一次自己張羅的生活感悟

zh-tw.content: 第一次自己張羅中元供品。三樣，超商買的，桌子是紙箱。沒人教過我，我還是走出去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合第一次自己準備拜拜的租屋族，發限動或跟朋友聊天用。
variations: 小時候我只負責拜完把餅乾搬走。今年，餅乾是我自己買的。
供品三樣、桌子一個紙箱。心意這種東西，本來就不用很大張。

en.content: First time putting out the offerings myself. Three things from the corner store, a cardboard box for a table. Nobody taught me. I went anyway.
en.editorNote: For anyone handling a family custom alone for the first time.
variations: As a kid my only job was carrying the snacks back inside. This year I bought the snacks.
Three items and a cardboard box. Sincerity was never supposed to need a big table.

items.sourceNote: 2026 七夕（8/19）日期與習俗介紹；改寫為成年伴侶的日常版浪漫

zh-tw.content:
七夕那天我們哪裡都沒去。

他清掉冰箱最底層那格，我把卡了半年的抽屜軌道弄順。晚餐自己煮，八點就吃完了。

二十幾歲會覺得這樣很可惜。現在覺得，大人的浪漫是家裡少一樣壞掉的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕沒有安排、但其實過得不錯的伴侶。
variations: 沒訂餐廳，沒買花。修好一個抽屜，兩個人都很有成就感。
浪漫的定義會改。以前是驚喜，現在是他記得我不吃香菜。

en.content:
We didn't go anywhere for Chinese Valentine's Day.

He cleared out the bottom shelf of the fridge. I finally got the drawer sliding again after six months of it sticking. We cooked, and we were done eating by eight.

At twenty-five that would have felt like a waste. Now it feels like the point: adult romance is one less broken thing in the house.
en.editorNote: For couples with no big plans who are secretly doing fine.
variations: No reservation, no flowers. One fixed drawer, two very satisfied people.
Romance gets redefined. It used to be surprises. Now it's him remembering what I won't eat.

items.sourceNote: 2026 上班族 AI 焦慮調查：多數人感受企業更看重 AI 能力；改寫為職涯規劃語感的變化

zh-tw.content: 以前的職涯規劃，是想十年後要坐上哪個位子。現在是算，這個技能還能撐幾年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最近在想轉職、或被公司要求學新工具的人。
variations: 以前怕升不上去，現在怕被留在原地也不行。
履歷上最舊的那一項技能，是我最不敢刪的那一項。

en.content: Career planning used to mean choosing the title I'd hold in ten years. Now it means estimating how many years this skill has left.
en.editorNote: For anyone eyeing a career change or being told to learn a new tool.
variations: I used to worry about not moving up. Now standing still isn't allowed either.
The oldest skill on my resume is the one I'm most afraid to delete.

items.sourceNote: 115 學年度行事曆：暑假 7/1-8/30、開學約 8/31；改寫為成年人靠他人行事曆感受季節

zh-tw.content:
月底一開學，早上的公車就會突然沒位子。

制服、書包、耳機線，整台車瞬間年輕十歲。

我沒有開學這件事很多年了，可是我的通勤時間，還是被別人的行事曆決定。

大人的季節感，是身邊的人幫你換的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學前一週的通勤族，發文或跟同事閒聊都好用。
variations: 我的季節不是看天氣，是看早上公車有沒有位子。
夏天結束的訊號，是站牌前面突然多出一排書包。

en.content:
Once school starts at the end of the month, the morning bus stops having seats.

Uniforms, backpacks, headphone cords. The whole bus drops ten years overnight.

I haven't had a first day of school in a very long time. My commute still runs on somebody else's calendar.

Adults get their sense of seasons secondhand, from the people around them.
en.editorNote: For commuters in the last week before school starts.
variations: I don't track seasons by weather. I track them by whether the bus has a seat.
Summer ends the morning a row of backpacks appears at the stop.

items.sourceNote: 燈具選購資料：多數人只看瓦數，但瓦數是耗電、亮度看流明，另有燈座與色溫；改寫為成年後才學會的採買常識

zh-tw.content: 換燈泡不難，難的是買對那顆。大人的第一步，是把壞的拆下來帶去店裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛搬出來自己住、第一次面對五金行的人。
variations: 燈座、色溫、流明，三個都要對，沒有人教過我。
現在我會先拍照再去買，這也算長大的一種。

en.content: Changing a bulb is easy. Buying the right one isn't. Step one of adulthood: take the dead one to the store.
en.editorNote: For anyone living alone for the first time and facing the hardware aisle.
variations: Base, color temp, lumens. Three things to get right, and nobody ever mentioned them.
Now I photograph it before I shop. That counts as growing up.

items.sourceNote: 路由器設定與斷線排除指南；改寫為成年人自學的唯一維修技能

zh-tw.content: 沒人教我怎麼修網路。斷線的時候，我拔插頭、數到三十、插回去——然後它就好了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在家工作、網路一斷就心跳加速的人。
variations: 我的維修技能只有一招，就是拔掉再插回去。
電腦、路由器、人，重開機這招都有效。

en.content: Nobody taught me how to fix the internet. When it drops, I unplug it, count to thirty, plug it back in. It works.
en.editorNote: For remote workers whose pulse spikes the second the wifi dies.
variations: My entire repair skill set is unplug it and plug it back in.
Laptops, routers, people. A restart helps all three.

items.sourceNote: 一個人住需要的生活技能討論；改寫為打客服電話的自學過程

zh-tw.content: 電話那頭念到第四個選項，我已經連按三次零。找真人這件事，是自學的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛跟電信、銀行、保險客服搏鬥完的人發文自嘲。
variations: 等候音樂聽到後來，我已經會跟著哼了。
大人的必修課，是聽完四個選項還沒掛掉。

en.content: By the fourth menu option I've already mashed zero three times. Reaching a human is a skill I taught myself.
en.editorNote: For anyone who just survived a call with their bank or phone company.
variations: I've been on hold so long I can hum the music now.
Adulthood is sitting through four menu options without hanging up.

items.sourceNote: 居家水電 DIY 課程報導提到民眾遇故障多半先付錢才學會處理；改寫為成年後的學費比喻

zh-tw.content: 這些事沒有人教，所以最後都是罰單、滯納金跟師傅的估價單在教。學費有點貴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛被繳費期限或維修報價教訓過的人。
variations: 我的成年教育學費，大部分繳給了滯納金。
沒人教的事，最後都會自己來跟你收費。

en.content: Nobody taught me any of this. The tickets, the late fees, and the repair quotes did. Tuition runs a little steep.
en.editorNote: For anyone who just got schooled by a due date or a repair estimate.
variations: Most of my adult education budget went to late fees.
The things nobody teaches you will eventually bill you themselves.

items.sourceNote: 報導談瑞典人下班後把工作群組靜音、台灣則是秒回也能升遷；改寫為成年人一天中唯一無人找得到的空檔

zh-tw.content: 等紅燈，倒數從十九跳到十八。這十九秒沒有人找得到我：手機在包包裡，公司還沒到，家裡的事還沒開始。小時候嫌等紅燈浪費時間，現在我希望它再長一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 通勤路上突然覺得那幾秒很珍貴時，可以配這段發限動。
variations: 我一天裡唯一沒人找我的時段，長度是十九秒。
以前趕著過馬路，現在偷偷希望下一個路口也是紅燈。

en.content: At the red light, the counter drops from nineteen to eighteen. For those nineteen seconds nobody can reach me — phone's in my bag, I'm not at the office yet, and the house hasn't started asking for anything. I used to think red lights were wasted time. Now I hope for a long one.
en.editorNote: Pair it with a commute photo when those few seconds suddenly feel valuable.
variations: The only stretch of my day when nobody wants anything from me is nineteen seconds long.
I used to race the crosswalk. Now I quietly hope the next light is red too.

items.sourceNote: 牙科衛教指出磨牙不只發生在夜間、白天清醒時也會緊咬，且與壓力高度相關；改寫為身體先替你承認壓力

zh-tw.content:
牙醫把鏡子轉過來給我看，後面那兩顆的邊緣已經磨平了。他說：「你晚上有在咬。」

我說我睡得很好啊。

他說，會咬的人都這樣講。

那天回家我才注意到，我坐在電腦前的時候，牙齒是咬著的；排隊結帳的時候也是。原來我白天就開始了，晚上只是比較用力。
zh-tw.editorNote: 看完牙或做完健檢想寫點什麼時用，也很適合傳給那個一直說自己還好的同事。
variations: 我以為壓力會有聲音，結果它只是安靜地把我的牙齒磨平。
我的身體比我誠實，它早就承認我最近不太好。

en.content:
The dentist swiveled the mirror around: the edges of my back two teeth were worn flat. He said, "You're clenching at night."

I told him I sleep fine.

He said everyone who clenches says that.

That evening I noticed my jaw was locked while I sat at my laptop, and locked again while I stood in the checkout line. Turns out I start during the day. At night I just press harder.
en.editorNote: For a post after a dental visit or a checkup — or for the coworker who keeps insisting they're fine.
variations: I assumed stress would make some kind of noise. It just quietly filed my teeth down.
My body is more honest than I am. It admitted I wasn't okay months ago.

items.sourceNote: 居家水電文章說明老屋管徑小、多處同時用水就會分流導致每個出水點都變弱；改寫為成年人精力分配的比喻

zh-tw.content:
大人的力氣像老公寓的水壓。

一個人洗澡是夠的。可是洗衣機一轉，廚房再開一個水龍頭，蓮蓬頭立刻變成用滴的。

不是水不見了，是同時要供的地方太多。

所以現在有人約我，我會先算今天還有幾個水龍頭開著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 想婉拒邀約又不想講得太硬的時候，這段拿來當開場白剛好。
variations: 我沒有變冷淡，我只是知道自己一次只能開一個水龍頭。
累的時候不是沒力，是每個地方都分到一點，哪裡都不夠用。

en.content:
An adult's energy works like the water pressure in an old apartment.

One person showering is fine. Start the washing machine, open the kitchen tap, and the showerhead drops to a drip.

The water didn't vanish. Too many places are drawing from it at once.

So when someone invites me out now, I count how many taps I already have running today.
en.editorNote: A soft opener for turning down an invitation without sounding cold.
variations: I didn't get colder. I just learned I can only run one tap at a time.
Being tired isn't having no energy. It's every part of your life getting a trickle.

items.sourceNote: 2026 職場心理安全感報導：高安全感團隊裡成員敢說「我不知道」而不被貼標籤；改寫為給後輩的第二人稱建議

zh-tw.content:
你不用在會議裡假裝聽懂。

講一次「這個我不確定，我查完回你」，然後真的在下班前回。天不會塌，對方反而會記得你是說到做到的人。

面子只能保護你到下一個問題，信用可以保護你很多年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 帶新人或跟後輩聊職場心態時可以直接引用。
variations: 我在職場上最有用的一句話是：「這個我不確定，我查完回你。」
會議裡點頭最快的人，通常是回信最慢的人。

en.content:
You don't have to fake understanding in meetings.

Say it once — "I'm not sure, let me check and get back to you" — and then actually get back to them before you leave for the day. Nothing collapses. What people remember is that you did what you said.

Saving face only protects you until the next question. A reputation protects you for years.
en.editorNote: Worth quoting when you're mentoring someone new to the workplace.
variations: The most useful line I have at work is: I'm not sure, let me check and get back to you.
The person who nods fastest in the meeting is usually the slowest to reply.

items.sourceNote: 2026 網路行為報告：手機拍照用途從紀錄生活轉向資訊備忘；改寫成第一人稱相簿盤點

zh-tw.content:
手機相簿滑到最後，是我這個月的生活紀錄：

停車場 B2 的柱子編號、藥盒背面那行成分、我媽健保卡的正反面、水表上的數字、租約裡寫押金的那一頁，還有一件我沒買、但想記住尺寸的外套。

沒有一張是為了以後拿出來看的。它們全部都是為了「等一下不要出事」。

大人的相簿其實是一本備忘錄，只是封面長得像回憶。
zh-tw.editorNote: 整理手機或跟朋友聊「你相簿裡最近都是什麼」時，很適合配這一則。
variations: 我相簿裡最新的十張照片，一個人都沒有。
大人拍照不是為了紀念，是為了不要忘記。

en.content:
Scroll to the end of my camera roll and you get my whole month:

The pillar number on level B2. The ingredients on the back of a pill bottle. Both sides of my mom's insurance card. The water meter. The page of the lease with the deposit on it. A jacket I didn't buy but wanted the size of.

Not one of them is meant to be looked at again someday. Every single one is there so nothing goes wrong later.

My camera roll is a to-do list wearing the cover of a photo album.
en.editorNote: Good caption for cleaning out your phone, or for a thread about what adults actually photograph.
variations: The last ten photos on my phone have zero people in them.
Adults don't take photos to remember the day. We take them because we know we'll forget.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 7-8 月苦茶油苯駢芘超標、多家品牌陸續下架回收的食安新聞；改寫成第一人稱「翻櫃子對批號」場景，不提品牌

zh-tw.content:
新聞跳出來的時候我在客廳，第一個動作是站起來走去廚房。

蹲在流理臺下面，把那瓶油翻過來，用手機照著瓶底那行小字，一個數字一個數字對。對完不是同一批，我鬆了一口氣，然後順手把後面那三瓶也拿出來看。

以前這種新聞我看完就滑掉了。那時候我沒有廚房，也沒有人吃我煮的東西。

現在有了。所以新聞對我來說已經不只是新聞，是一件我今天要去確認的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 食安或商品回收上新聞的那幾天，很適合拿來當貼文開頭。
variations: 以前看到下架新聞是滑過去，現在是站起來走去廚房。
長大就是從「聽說有事」變成「我去確認一下」。

en.content:
The recall alert popped up while I was on the couch, and the first thing I did was stand up and walk into the kitchen.

I crouched under the sink, turned the bottle over, held my phone up to the tiny line of print on the bottom, and matched the lot number digit by digit. Different batch. I exhaled, and then pulled out the three bottles behind it and checked those too.

I used to scroll past this kind of news. Back then I didn't have a kitchen, and nobody ate anything I cooked.

Now they do. So the news isn't just news anymore. It's something I have to go verify today.
en.editorNote: Works as an opener whenever a food recall or product safety story is going around.
variations: I used to scroll past recall news. Now I stand up and go check the kitchen.
Growing up is the day "I heard something happened" turns into "let me go check."

items.sourceNote: 1111 人力銀行 2026 青年上班族轉職調查：35 歲以下 30.8% 每天都想離職；改寫成面試反問環節的個人視角

zh-tw.content:
面試的最後，對方問：你有什麼想問我們的嗎？

二十五歲的我會問：這個職位的發展性如何？我可以學到什麼？

現在我問的是：這個位置上一個人待多久、為什麼走？團隊平均幾點離開辦公室？請假要幾天前提出？

我還是想學東西。只是我現在知道，讓人撐不下去的原因，從來不會寫在職務說明上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 轉職季或朋友在準備面試時可以丟給他，當成提醒。
variations: 面試最後那句「你有什麼想問的」，年紀愈大問得愈具體。
以前面試問能學到什麼，現在問前一個人為什麼走。

en.content:
End of the interview: "Do you have any questions for us?"

At twenty-five I asked about growth paths and what I'd get to learn.

Now I ask how long the last person lasted and why they left, what time the team actually goes home, and how far ahead I need to request time off.

I still want to learn things. I've just found out that the reason people burn out never shows up in the job description.
en.editorNote: Send it to a friend prepping for interviews, or post it during hiring season.
variations: The older I get, the more specific my questions get at the end of an interview.
I used to ask what I'd learn. Now I ask why the last person left.

items.sourceNote: 上班族日常疲勞相關報導；改寫成飯後拖延洗碗的第一人稱笑點

zh-tw.content:
吃完飯，碗在桌上，我在椅子上。

我們互相看著，誰都沒有動。而我很清楚接下來會發生什麼：我會說等一下洗，然後去洗澡、躺平、滑一輪手機，等到凌晨想起來的時候，那個碗已經在水槽裡自己變成一件更難的事。

大人的懶惰是有利息的，而且都是隔天的自己在還。
zh-tw.editorNote: 深夜發文或跟室友、伴侶互相取笑家事時很好用。
variations: 十分鐘的家事，我可以用三個小時來逃避。
碗不會因為你多看它兩眼就自己洗好，但我每天都試一次。

en.content:
Dinner's over. The plates are on the table. I'm in the chair.

We look at each other. Neither of us moves. And I know exactly how this goes: I say I'll do them later, I shower, I lie down, I scroll for a while, and by the time I remember at one in the morning, the sink has quietly turned them into a harder job.

Procrastination charges interest, and it's always tomorrow's version of you who pays it.
en.editorNote: Good for a late-night post, or for roasting a roommate or partner about chores.
variations: A ten-minute chore that I can avoid for three hours.
Staring at the dishes has never once washed them, and yet I try daily.

items.sourceNote: 報導指每 4 位勞工就有 1 人下班後仍需數位待命、看到主管訊息就緊張；改寫成上班時段收到一句「有空聊一下」的內心小劇場

zh-tw.content:
快下班的時候，主管傳來四個字：有空聊一下。

接下來的十二分鐘，我在腦中把最壞的版本演完了三遍——上個月那個案子出包、要調組、公司要縮編，我甚至已經算到存款可以撐幾個月。

走進去，他頭也沒抬就問：那份報表第三欄，你當初是抓哪一段時間？

我回座位坐下來，手心還是濕的，那十二分鐘沒有人派給我，是我自己加的班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次看到主管私訊就心臟一縮的同事；也很適合週一開工時發。
variations: 主管說「有空聊一下」，我的腦袋自動幫他補完了整段離職面談。
我這禮拜最累的十二分鐘，發生在走去主管座位的路上。

en.content:
Ten minutes before I log off, four words from my manager: got a sec?

Over the next twelve minutes I ran the worst version three times — last month's project blew up, they're moving me to another team, the company's cutting headcount. I got as far as counting how many months my savings would cover.

I walk in and he asks without looking up: that third column in the report, what date range did you pull?

I sat back down with damp palms. Nobody assigned me those twelve minutes. I put in that overtime myself.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker whose stomach drops every time the manager DMs them.
variations: "Got a sec?" and my brain has already written the whole exit interview.
The most exhausting twelve minutes of my week happened on the walk to my boss's desk.

items.sourceNote: 2026 夏月電價 6-9 月適用、家庭用電採累進費率的報導；改寫成捨不得換掉舊電扇的第一人稱場景，不提電價數字

zh-tw.content:
客廳那台電扇轉起來會喀、喀、喀，聽久了很像有人在旁邊小聲說「我盡量」。

弱風那一段按下去它會裝作沒聽到，搖頭的角度只剩一半，可是最熱的那半個月它一次都沒有停過。

我查過同款新的九百塊，也在店裡站著看了兩次，兩次都空手走出來。

每年八月我都想著要換掉它，每年九月它都還在轉，我們就這樣一起撐到了第十個夏天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配一張自家老電器的照片發文，或傳給那個什麼都捨不得丟的家人。
variations: 家裡最資深的員工是那台電扇，年年考績都低空飛過，年年續約。
它只剩兩段風可以用，但那兩段撐過了我整個夏天。

en.content:
The fan in my living room clicks as it turns — click, click, click — and after a while it sounds like someone quietly saying "I'm trying."

Press the low setting and it pretends not to hear you, and it only sweeps half as far as it used to, but through the hottest two weeks of the year it never once quit.

A new one of the same model runs about thirty bucks, and I've stood in the store looking at it twice and walked out empty-handed both times.

Every August I decide to replace it, every September it's still spinning, and that's ten summers the two of us have made it through.
en.editorNote: Pair it with a photo of your oldest appliance, or send it to the relative who never throws anything away.
variations: My longest-serving employee is a fan with two working speeds.
It barely works and it has never let me down. Those are not a contradiction.

items.sourceNote: 2026 訂房平台攻略提醒付款前確認取消期限、總價、加收費用等六項；改寫成初級／高級大人的訂房對照

zh-tw.content:
初級大人訂房，看的是照片好不好看、床大不大、有沒有浴缸。

高級大人訂房，先滑到最下面看退訂規則，再翻三頁評論找有沒有人提到隔音，最後打開地圖量到車站要走幾分鐘。

這些習慣全部都是繳過學費的：有一年隔壁房唱歌唱到兩點，有一年臨時退訂被扣六成，還有一年拖著行李在太陽底下走了二十五分鐘。

大人的旅行從按下訂房那一刻就開始了，而最花力氣的部分，多半發生在還沒出門以前。
zh-tw.editorNote: 揪團旅行、大家在群組挑住宿的時候丟出來，負責訂房的那個人會很有感。
variations: 以前挑住宿看夜景，現在挑住宿看退訂條款。
群組裡負責訂房的那個人，通常是全團最早開始旅行的人。

en.content:
Junior adult books a hotel: nice photos, big bed, is there a tub.

Senior adult books a hotel: scrolls straight down to the cancellation policy, reads three pages of reviews hunting for the words "thin walls," then measures the walk to the station on the map.

Every one of those habits came with tuition — one year the room next door sang until two, one year a last-minute cancellation cost me sixty percent, one year I dragged a suitcase twenty-five minutes in full sun.

An adult's trip starts the second you hit book, and most of the effort happens before anyone leaves the house.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the group chat while everyone's arguing over where to stay.
variations: I used to pick hotels by the view. Now I pick them by the refund window.
Whoever books the rooms is always the first person on the trip.

items.sourceNote: 中華郵政臨櫃業務多須備妥證件、印章與影本的須知；改寫成第一人稱「一次就辦成」的小成就感

zh-tw.content:
早上去郵局，抽完號碼牌我又把資料夾打開檢查一次：身分證、印章、影本兩份，還有一張我猜他們可能會問、所以順手夾進去的舊帳單。

叫到號，五分鐘辦完，櫃檯小姐抬頭說了一句：你準備得很齊喔。

走出自動門，外面太陽很大，我居然有一點得意。

這種成就感很小，小到不能跟任何人講，但它確實是我這個禮拜最順利的一件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 辦完事走出來心情很好的時候發，或用來鼓勵剛開始自己跑流程的新鮮人。
variations: 大人的高光時刻：文件帶齊，一次辦成，不用再跑第二趟。
沒有人會替你鼓掌，但你自己知道那份資料夾整理了多久。

en.content:
Took a number at the post office this morning and opened my folder one more time: ID, seal, two photocopies, plus an old bill I tossed in because I had a hunch they'd ask.

They called my number, it took five minutes, and the clerk looked up and said, you came prepared.

I walked out into the glare weirdly pleased with myself.

It's a tiny kind of pride, too small to tell anyone about, and it was still the smoothest thing that happened to me all week.
en.editorNote: Post it after an errand goes right, or send it to someone learning to handle their own paperwork.
variations: Peak adulthood: every document in hand, done in one trip.
Nobody claps for this, but you know how long that folder took to put together.

items.sourceNote: 勞保局勞工自願提繳退休金相關規定，以及 2026 年 8 月起雇主不得拒絕代為申報自提的新制；改寫成第一人稱看薪資單的前後對照

zh-tw.content:
剛換工作那半年，薪資單寄來我只看最下面那一格，看完就關掉。

今天我把整份滑到底，停在「自願提繳」那四個字上面，欄位裡是一個零。

我算了一下，六趴大概是我一個月兩次外食加一趟計程車，然後把那個零改成六。

同一份薪資單，那時候我看的是這個月能花多少，現在我看的是六十歲的我能領多少。
zh-tw.editorNote: 發薪日或年度財務盤點的時候發，也適合丟給還沒點開過那一欄的同事。
variations: 同一張薪資單，二十五歲看的是實領，三十五歲看的是提繳。
把那個零改成六的那天，我才算真的替未來的自己排了一次班。

en.content:
In my first months at the new job, my pay stub showed up and I looked at exactly one number, the one at the bottom.

Today I scrolled all the way down and stopped on the line marked voluntary contribution, where the field said zero.

I ran the math, worked out that six percent costs me two dinners out and one cab ride a month, and typed a six over that zero.

Same pay stub, and back then I was reading it for what I could spend this month while now I read it for what I collect at sixty.
en.editorNote: Good for payday, or for the coworker who has never opened that part of their pay stub.
variations: At twenty-five you read the take-home line, and at thirty-five you read the contribution line.
Changing that zero to a six was the first shift I ever scheduled for my future self.

items.sourceNote: 床墊約七到十年需更換、支撐性下降與晨起腰背不適的衛教說明；改寫成以床墊為敘事者的擬人視角

zh-tw.content:
我是你七年前用第一筆年終買的那張床墊，你當時連躺都沒躺，看到打折就刷了。

前三年你回家倒下就睡，最近你會先坐在我邊邊滑很久手機，再慢慢躺下來。

你翻身的次數變多了，早上起來會扶一下腰，這個月還跑去三家店躺過新的，躺完每次都說再想想。

我知道你在等一個更好的價錢，可是你的腰在等的，是一個願意把錢花在自己身上的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 腰痠背痛、或是一件該換的東西一直下不了手的時候拿出來提醒自己。
variations: 床墊會老，你的腰不會等它降價。
拖最久沒換的那一樣，通常是最每天在用的那一樣。

en.content:
I'm the mattress you bought seven years ago with your first bonus, without lying down on me once, because the sale ended that night.

For three years you dropped straight onto me and slept, and lately you sit on my edge scrolling for a while before you ease yourself down.

You turn over more than you used to, you reach for your lower back in the morning, and this month you tried three showroom beds and told all three of them you would think about it.

I know you're waiting for a better price, and what your back is waiting for is a version of you who spends money on yourself.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend whose back hurts and who keeps postponing the one purchase that would help.
variations: Mattresses wear out, and your spine is not going to wait for a sale.
The thing you put off replacing the longest is usually the thing you use every single day.

items.sourceNote: 壽險保單滿期給付與通知流程的一般說明；改寫成誤以為是催繳文件、拆開才發現是家人多年前投保的翻轉

zh-tw.content:
信箱裡躺著一張掛號信通知單，我盯著寄件人那一欄看了很久，腦中已經先把可能欠的錢排過一輪。

隔天去領，簽名的時候手還有點僵，回到車上才敢拆。

裡面是一張滿期通知：我十八歲那年家裡幫我保的儲蓄險，今年繳完了，錢會匯進我的戶頭。

我坐在車上打電話回家，那頭很平淡地說忘記跟你講，好像存二十年在他們那邊就是一件順手的小事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 想起家人默默做過什麼、或收到意料之外的好消息時發。
variations: 有些人愛你的方式，是繳了二十年保費都沒跟你講一聲。
拆信封之前先深呼吸，你猜的通常比事實嚴重很多。

en.content:
There was a certified mail slip in my box, and I stared at the sender line long enough to mentally list everything I might owe.

I picked it up the next day, signed with a stiff hand, and waited until I was back in the car to open it.

Inside was a maturity notice for a savings policy my family started the year I turned eighteen, fully paid off now, with the money heading to my account.

I called home from the parking lot and they said they forgot to mention it, like twenty years of premiums had been a small errand on their end.
en.editorNote: For the day a family member's quiet effort finally turns up in your mailbox.
variations: Some people love you by paying premiums for twenty years and never bringing it up.
Take a breath before you open the envelope, because what you imagined is usually worse than what's inside.

items.sourceNote: 機車鉛酸電瓶壽命約二到四年、常無預警失效的一般說明；改寫成機車行對話與「沒人交接」的成人隱喻

zh-tw.content:
早上按了三次都沒反應，我牽著車走了兩條街到機車行。

老闆蹲下去看了兩秒，抬頭問我「上次換電瓶是什麼時候」。

我說不知道，這台是二手接手的，前一個車主什麼都沒交代。

他一邊拆一邊說「大人的東西都嘛這樣，接的時候沒人講，壞掉那天你才知道自己接了什麼」，然後報了一個比我以為的還便宜的價錢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 車子或家電突然罷工那天發，也適合送給剛接手一堆沒人交代的事的人。
variations: 大人的世界沒有交接單，壞掉那天就是你的到職日。
沒人告訴你上一個人做過什麼，你都是從故障開始認識它。

en.content:
It wouldn't start after three tries, so I pushed the scooter two blocks to the repair shop.

The owner crouched down, looked at it for about two seconds, and asked when I last replaced the battery.

I told him I had no idea, that I bought the bike used and the previous owner never mentioned a thing.

He said adult life runs about the same way, nobody hands you notes and you find out what you inherited on the day it quits, and then he quoted me less than I expected.
en.editorNote: Good for the day something breaks, or for anyone who just inherited a job nobody explained.
variations: Nobody leaves you a handover doc, so the day it breaks is your first day.
You meet most of your responsibilities for the first time on the day they stop working.

items.sourceNote: 成年後社交圈萎縮（friendship recession）的一般討論；改寫成社區停電那晚在中庭認識鄰居的自問自答

zh-tw.content:
有人問我上一次交到新朋友是什麼時候，我認真想了很久。

答案是去年夏天整棟大樓停電的那個晚上，所有人都下來坐在中庭等電力公司。

三個小時裡，我知道了五樓那對夫妻姓什麼、三樓阿姨的狗幾歲、哪一戶有一台手搖式收音機。

長大以後認識人變得很被動，得先有一件麻煩的事，把大家湊到同一個地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 跟朋友聊到「長大後到底怎麼交朋友」的時候發，也適合停電或社區出事那天。
variations: 長大以後的友情，多半是從一場共同的麻煩開始的。
停電三小時，我認識的鄰居比住進來三年還多。

en.content:
Someone asked me when I last made a new friend, and it took me a long minute to come up with anything.

The answer is the night the whole building lost power last summer and everyone ended up in the courtyard waiting on the utility company.

In three hours I learned the last name of the couple on five, the age of the dog on three, and which unit still owned a hand-crank radio.

Meeting people as an adult is a passive sport, where something has to go wrong before anybody stands in the same place long enough.
en.editorNote: For the conversation about how adults are supposed to make friends at all.
variations: Most adult friendships start with a shared inconvenience.
Three hours without power and I met more neighbors than in three years of living here.

items.sourceNote: 職場疲勞與「累了也沒跟人講」的討論風向；改寫成早餐店老闆娘旁觀常客的第三人視角

zh-tw.content:
我今天把那個聊天視窗打開了三次。

前兩次連一個字都沒打就退出來。第三次真的打了，一句很短的，說我最近有點撐不住。手指停在送出鍵上面，停到螢幕自己暗掉。

再亮起來的時候，我把那行字一個一個刪乾淨，退出去，鎖螢幕。

然後低頭繼續吃那碗已經涼掉的麵，一邊想明天要幾點起床。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種話都打好了卻按不下送出的晚上，也適合傳給最近安靜得有點反常的人。
variations: 打好的那句話沒送出去，最後是被自己刪掉的。
累到最後連講出來都嫌麻煩，乾脆先去把麵吃完。

en.content:
I opened that chat window three times today.

The first two times I backed out without typing anything. The third time I actually wrote it, one short line, saying I'm not holding up so well lately. My thumb sat on send until the screen went dark on its own.

When it lit up again I deleted the line character by character, backed out, locked the phone.

Then I went back to the bowl of noodles that had gone cold, working out what time I'd have to get up tomorrow.
en.editorNote: For the nights when the message is written and never sent; also for the person who has gone unusually quiet.
variations: The message got written. It just got deleted instead of sent.
Too tired to explain it, so I finished the noodles instead.

items.sourceNote: adulting 讓人學會隱藏情緒、硬撐日常的評論；改寫成替「習慣就好」下的非字典定義

zh-tw.content:
二十二歲，主管說這行就是這樣，習慣就好。我回家跟室友抱怨到半夜兩點，隔天眼睛腫著去上班。

二十八歲，換我對坐隔壁的新人講出一樣的話，講完自己愣了兩秒。

三十五歲，健檢報告的紅字多了兩行，醫生問我最近壓力大不大，我說還好，就那樣。

走出診間的時候，手機跳出下午兩點的會議提醒，我加快腳步。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近問他什麼都回「還好」的朋友。
variations: 二十二歲聽到習慣就好會抱怨到半夜，二十八歲換自己講出口。
醫生問我壓力大不大，我說還好，然後趕去開會。

en.content:
At 22, my boss told me that's just how this industry runs, you get used to it. I complained to my roommate until two in the morning and turned up the next day with swollen eyes.

At 28, the same line came out of my own mouth, pointed at the new hire in the next seat. I sat there for a beat after I said it.

At 35, the health screening came back with two more numbers flagged in red. The doctor asked whether work had been stressful lately. I said it was fine, about the usual.

On my way out of the clinic my phone lit up with the 2pm meeting reminder, and I picked up the pace.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's been answering everything with "I'm fine" lately.
variations: At 22 that line kept me up till two. At 28 I was the one saying it.
The doctor asked about stress. I said fine, then hurried off to a meeting.

items.sourceNote: adulting 世代「暫時扮演大人」的討論；改寫成尚未發生但必然到來的家族聚餐結帳場面

zh-tw.content:
總有一天，家族吃完飯站起來的那一刻，先走向櫃檯的人會是你。

長輩會在後面喊你回來，說哪有讓晚輩付的道理，你會笑著揮揮手，把單子壓在手心裡。

那頓飯不會特別貴，也不會有人拍照，隔天大概沒有人記得吃了什麼。

可是按下確認鍵的時候你會心跳一下，那一下跟金額沒什麼關係，比較像有人在旁邊提醒你，這張桌子的位置已經換過了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合家族聚餐當天發，或送給第一次搶著結帳的人。
variations: 有一天你會先站起來走去櫃檯，那天不會有人事先通知你。
長大的其中一個瞬間，是你把單子壓在手心裡，笑著說這餐我來。

en.content:
One of these nights, when the family meal winds down, you'll be the one who stands up first and heads for the register.

Someone older will call after you about how it isn't right to let the young one pay, and you'll wave them off with the check already folded in your hand.

It won't be an expensive dinner, nobody will photograph it, and by the next day no one will remember what was ordered.

Still, your heart will knock once when you tap to confirm, less about the amount than about the seats around that table quietly changing hands.
en.editorNote: Good for family dinner night, or for whoever just picked up the check for the first time.
variations: One day you'll be the one walking to the register, and nobody warns you it's your turn.
Growing up is partly the moment you fold the check into your palm and say you've got this one.

items.sourceNote: 外媒網友分享「意識到自己是大人」的瞬間；改寫成診所候診區等叫號時的一段時間差

zh-tw.content:
候診螢幕跳到我前面兩號，我正把健保卡從卡套裡摳出來。

摳到一半手指停住，改去滑開手機，把一張擺了三個月的停車費繳款單找出來繳掉。

護理師喊到名字，我站起來，順手把坐熱的椅子推正。

走進診間前那三秒，我想起小時候是誰牽著我坐在同一排椅子上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看診當天發，或送給第一次自己去掛號的人。
variations: 健保卡還沒摳出來，我先把擺了三個月的繳款單繳掉了。
站起來的時候順手把椅子推正，這個動作是什麼時候學會的。

en.content:
The waiting room screen jumps to two numbers before mine, and I'm halfway through prying my insurance card out of its sleeve.

My fingers stop, and I unlock my phone instead to finally pay a parking notice that has been sitting there for three months.

A nurse calls my name, I stand, and I straighten the chair I just warmed up.

In the three seconds before I reach the exam room, I remember who used to hold my hand in that same row of chairs.
en.editorNote: For appointment day, or for whoever just booked their own first visit.
variations: Card still stuck in its sleeve, and I'd already paid off a three-month-old parking notice.
I straightened the chair on my way up. No idea when I picked that up.

items.sourceNote: 台灣寫作平台上「意識到自己長大的瞬間」隨筆；改寫成同一間自習室、相隔十年的兩次落座

zh-tw.content:
高三那年我為了搶市圖三樓自習室靠窗的位子，七點半就去門口排隊。

十年後我又坐回同一張桌子，包裡裝的是筆電和一份要在今晚寄出去的交接清單。

桌角那道刻痕還在，當年我嫌它卡筆，現在我會一邊想事情一邊用拇指去按它。

同樣的日光燈打下來，差別在那時候有人會傳訊息問我幾點回家吃飯。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回母校或回舊自習室那天發，也適合離職前一晚。
variations: 十年前為了靠窗的位子排隊，十年後帶著筆電坐回同一張桌子。
日光燈還是那盞，只有那個問我幾點回家吃飯的人不在了。

en.content:
Senior year of high school, I lined up outside the public library at seven thirty just to get the window seat in the third-floor study room.

Ten years later I'm back at the same table, except my bag holds a laptop and a handover checklist due tonight.

The scratch on the corner is still there. Back then it caught my pen and annoyed me; now I press it with my thumb while I think.

Same fluorescent light overhead. The difference is that back then someone would text to ask what time I was coming home for dinner.
en.editorNote: For the day you revisit an old campus or study room, or the night before you leave a job.
variations: Queued at seven thirty for that window seat once. Came back ten years later with a laptop.
Same table, same fluorescent light, nobody texting to ask when I'll be home for dinner.

items.sourceNote: 外媒「我真的是大人了」時刻整理；改寫成一個人逛夜市那兩小時的時刻表

zh-tw.content:
18:40　下班直接騎車到夜市，路上跟自己說今天不吃超商。
19:05　站在蚵仔煎攤前兩分鐘，先看完價目表才決定要吃什麼。
19:18　點了一份，加了蛋，沒有再算那五十塊要從哪一格扣。
19:36　吃到一半家裡打來，問我機車強制險到期了沒。
19:52　邊走邊回訊息，手上那杯木瓜牛奶已經退冰。
20:10　在套圈圈攤子前停了十秒，最後往停車的方向走。
20:44　到家把安全帽掛好，才想起剛剛沒去吃真正想吃的那攤。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人逛夜市的晚上發，或收工後想給自己一頓熱的時候。
variations: 19:18 點了一份加蛋，沒有再算那五十塊要從哪一格扣。
20:44 到家掛好安全帽，才想起沒去吃真正想吃的那攤。

en.content:
6:40pm　Rode straight to the night market after work, promising myself no convenience store dinner tonight.
7:05pm　Stood at the oyster omelet stall for two minutes, reading the whole price board before deciding.
7:18pm　Ordered one, added the egg, didn't stop to work out which budget line the extra fifty came from.
7:36pm　Family called mid-meal to ask whether my scooter insurance had expired.
7:52pm　Typed a reply while walking. The papaya milk in my other hand had gone warm.
8:10pm　Paused ten seconds at the ring toss booth, then kept walking toward where I'd parked.
8:44pm　Hung up my helmet at home and realized I never got to the stall I actually came for.
en.editorNote: For a solo night market run, or any evening you decide you deserve something hot.
variations: 7:18pm — ordered it with the egg, no mental math about which budget it came out of.
8:44pm — home, helmet hung up, and I never made it to the stall I came for.

items.sourceNote: 台灣論壇新手木工詢問螺絲規格與引孔；改寫成一張自己填的五金行代購申請單

zh-tw.content:
申請項目：一根跟壞掉那根長得一模一樣的螺絲
現況說明：椅子右後腳已經自己轉開兩次，我用衛生紙塞著撐了三個月
攜帶物品：拆下來的舊螺絲一根，裝在藥袋裡帶來
規格：不知道，我連公制英制都分不出來
預算上限：三十元，含一支可能用不到的十字起子
希望完成時間：今天晚上，因為明天有人要來坐那張椅子
備註：如果這次還是修不好，至少我學會了下次要先問什麼
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合修東西修到一半發，或送給第一次自己走進五金行的人。
variations: 規格欄我只能填「不知道」，但我把舊螺絲裝在藥袋裡帶來了。
預算三十元，含一支可能用不到的十字起子。

en.content:
Requesting: one screw that looks exactly like the broken one
Current situation: the chair's back right leg has worked itself loose twice; I've had tissue paper jammed in there for three months
Items brought: the old screw, carried here in a pharmacy bag
Spec: no idea, I can't even tell metric from imperial
Budget: thirty dollars, including a screwdriver I may never use
Needed by: tonight, because someone is sitting in that chair tomorrow
Notes: if this doesn't fix it, at least I now know what to ask first next time
en.editorNote: For a repair job halfway done, or for whoever just walked into a hardware store alone.
variations: Spec: no idea. But I brought the old screw in a pharmacy bag.
Budget: thirty dollars, including a screwdriver I may never use.

items.sourceNote: 自助洗車場改計時收費、半小時六十元無限用的新聞討論；取「投幣洗車捨不得慢慢洗」的心情改寫成兩個時間點對照

zh-tw.content:
大學那年第一次去自助洗車場，我投了三十塊就急著把泡沫沖掉，怕機器停了那筆錢就白花。

上個月又去，我先繞著車走一圈，哪裡有鳥屎、哪裡卡了泥沙都看過才投幣。

泡沫掛在車身上慢慢往下流的那半分鐘，我站在旁邊什麼都沒做。

一樣的三十塊，那時候買的是趕快結束，現在買的是那半分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合洗完車坐在駕駛座發呆時發，或送給開始捨得把一件小事做完的人。
variations: 以前投三十塊是為了趕快沖完，現在投三十塊是為了站在旁邊看泡沫流下來。
同樣三十塊，我終於買得起那半分鐘什麼都不做。

en.content:
The first time I used a coin-op car wash in college, I dropped in my coins and blasted the foam off immediately, terrified the timer would eat my money.

Last month I went back and walked a full lap around the car first, noting the bird droppings and the caked-on grit, before putting a single coin in.

For the thirty seconds the foam sat there sliding down the paint, I just stood and watched it.

Same handful of coins. Back then I was buying a quick finish. Now I'm buying those thirty seconds.
en.editorNote: For sitting in the driver's seat after a wash, or for anyone learning to let a small task take its time.
variations: I used to rinse the foam off fast. Now I stand there and let it run.
Same coins. These days they buy me thirty seconds of doing nothing.

items.sourceNote: 8/23 處暑遇農曆七月的節氣報導，取「季節換過去、自己還在同一個位置」的時間感；寫成理髮店的兩個時間點對照

zh-tw.content:
小學的時候我媽帶我去家附近那間家庭理髮，一百塊，我坐在一塊墊高的木板上，剪完直接回家寫功課。

昨天我自己走進一間店，設計師問我這次還是一樣嗎，我說一樣就好。

吹完頭我在櫃檯排了下一次的時間，順手記進行事曆，比上一次晚了兩個禮拜。

同一個髮型剪了二十年，中間換掉的是那個決定要不要改的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剪完頭髮走出店門那一刻發，或送給發現自己開始替自己做決定的人。
variations: 以前是我媽決定我剪什麼頭，現在是我自己選了同一個答案。
髮型二十年沒變，變的是誰在櫃檯付錢、誰在排下一次。

en.content:
In grade school my mom took me to the little neighborhood barbershop. A hundred bucks, a booster board across the armrests, and straight home to do homework after.

Yesterday I walked into a salon by myself, and when the stylist asked if I wanted the usual, I said the usual is fine.

After the blow-dry I booked my next slot at the counter and put it in my calendar, two weeks later than last time.

Twenty years of the same haircut. What changed is who gets to decide whether to change it.
en.editorNote: For the moment you step back onto the street after a haircut, or for anyone noticing they now make their own calls.
variations: My mom used to pick my haircut. Now I pick it, and I pick the same one.
Same haircut for twenty years. Different person paying at the counter.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 心情版討論「為什麼二手版都是九成新的鞋」，取三分鐘熱度賣掉裝備的窘境，改寫成二手刊登文

zh-tw.content:
品名：一雙只穿去跑過四次的慢跑鞋
購入原因：健檢報告多了兩行紅字，當天晚上就下單
狀況：鞋底左邊磨得比右邊多一點，其餘九成新
瑕疵：鞋盒被我拿去裝雜物，四個角都有壓痕
附贈：沒開封的運動水壺，還有我自己排的一週跑步表
售價：可議，面交自取
備註：鞋子沒問題，問題是我每次都把它排在一天的最後一件事
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合清鞋櫃清到一半發，或送給買了裝備卻一直沒開始的人。
variations: 瑕疵欄我只能誠實寫：鞋子九成新，因為我只穿去跑過四次。
附贈一份我自己排的跑步表，上面只打勾了四天。

en.content:
Item: one pair of running shoes, worn for exactly four runs
Why I bought them: two red lines on a health check report, ordered that same night
Condition: left sole slightly more worn than the right, otherwise like new
Flaws: I used the box for storage, so all four corners are dented
Included: an unopened sports bottle and the weekly running plan I wrote myself
Price: negotiable, local pickup
Notes: nothing wrong with the shoes. The problem is I kept scheduling them last in the day
en.editorNote: For a half-cleaned shoe rack, or for whoever bought the gear and never started.
variations: Flaws: none on the shoes. They've only been out four times.
Comes with the running plan I wrote. Four boxes ticked.

items.sourceNote: 強制險忘記續保會被罰一千五、逾期加重到三千的報導；改寫成兩人加油站前的對話

zh-tw.content:
「你機車強制險什麼時候到期？」
「不知道欸，那個會自動續約吧？」
「不會。去年我也以為會，然後收到一張一千五的罰單。」
「那等一下去加油站順便問？」
「加油站不辦這個啦，線上五分鐘就好。」
「五分鐘的事，我可以拖三個月。」
「我也是，通常拖到罰單寄來那天，才會突然變得很有效率。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在群組裡提醒朋友續保時丟出來，或送給總是拖到最後一天的人。
variations: 「線上五分鐘就好。」「五分鐘的事，我可以拖三個月。」
大人的待辦事項裡，最久沒動的那一件，通常只要五分鐘。

en.content:
"When does your scooter insurance expire?"
"No clue. Doesn't it auto-renew?"
"It does not. I assumed that last year and got a fine in the mail."
"Can I just ask at the gas station later?"
"They don't handle it. It takes five minutes online."
"Five minutes. I can stall that for three months."
"Same. I only get efficient the day the fine shows up."
en.editorNote: For nudging a friend in the group chat about renewals, or for anyone who waits until the last day.
variations: "It takes five minutes online." "Five minutes? I can stall that for three months."
The oldest thing on an adult's to-do list is usually a five-minute job.

items.sourceNote: 連鎖剪髮調漲、美髮業成本上升的報導；改寫成坐在剪髮椅上正在發生的一段內心戲

zh-tw.content:
設計師正把我頭髮撥開，問我這裡要不要打薄一點。

我看著鏡子裡的自己在點頭，其實我沒真的在聽，我在算今天這一趟比上次多了五十塊，然後想起去年我還會為了這五十塊多騎兩條街去別家。

剪刀在耳朵旁邊喀喀響，圍布底下我的手正在滑手機，把明天要交的東西再檢查一次。

鏡子裡那個人看起來很放鬆，只有我知道他腦袋裡在跑什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剪完頭髮走出店門那一刻發限動，或送給每次坐上那張椅子就開始想工作的人。
variations: 剪刀在耳朵旁邊響，我在圍布底下把明天的事又想了一遍。
長大的其中一個證據，是你能在最放鬆的椅子上，把最緊的事情想完。

en.content:
The stylist is fanning out my hair right now, asking if I want it thinned here.

I'm watching myself nod in the mirror, not really listening, because I'm doing the math on the extra fifty this cut costs compared to last time — and remembering when I'd have ridden two streets over to save exactly that.

The scissors keep clicking near my ear while my hand, hidden under the cape, scrolls through tomorrow's deadline one more time.

The guy in the mirror looks completely relaxed, and I'm the only one who knows what's running behind his eyes.
en.editorNote: For the moment you walk out of the salon, or for anyone whose brain starts working the second they sit down to relax.
variations: Scissors clicking by my ear, and under the cape I'm rehearsing tomorrow.
One sign you grew up: you can think your tightest thoughts in the most relaxing chair in town.

items.sourceNote: 犬貓美容服務定型化契約修正上路、消費糾紛與疑似棄養通報下降的報導；改寫成飼主站在店外玻璃窗前寫給狗的一封短信

zh-tw.content:
隔著這片玻璃，你被抱上檯子的那一秒整個身體僵住了，我在外面看得一清二楚。

你不會知道我為了今天先看過三家店的服務條款，挑到把該寫的都寫清楚的那一家，才敢把你交出去，也不會知道我剛剛在櫃檯把你會過敏那件事講了兩次。

你只會記得吹風機很吵、有人捏你的腳趾。

等一下你出來，我還是會被你撲一身水，然後我會蹲下去說你好棒，那句話有一半是講給我自己聽的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在毛小孩洗完澡的照片下面，或送給第一次把寵物交給別人照顧、在店外站到腿痠的飼主。
variations: 你只記得吹風機很吵，我記得我在玻璃外面站了一個小時。
把一個不會說話的家人交出去，是我學會的其中一種長大。

en.content:
Through this window I can see the exact second they lift you onto the table and your whole body goes stiff.

You'll never know that I read the service terms at three different shops before today and picked the one that spelled everything out, or that I told the front desk twice about the thing you're allergic to.

All you'll remember is that the dryer was loud and somebody squeezed your toes.

In a few minutes you'll come out and soak my shirt jumping on me, and I'll crouch down and tell you how brave you were, and half of that sentence will be for me.
en.editorNote: For the caption under your freshly groomed pet's photo, or for anyone leaving their animal with a stranger for the first time.
variations: You'll remember the loud dryer; I'll remember standing outside that window for an hour.
Handing over a family member who can't speak for himself is one of the ways I grew up.

items.sourceNote: 2026 台灣銀行營業時間整理（臨櫃只到平日下午三點半）的資料；改寫成請半天假坐在銀行等候區的假設語氣獨白

zh-tw.content:
如果二十二歲的我知道，有一天我請半天假是為了坐在銀行等候區辦完一份文件，大概會覺得這種大人很沒意思。

如果臨櫃時間再晚一小時，我今天就不必把整個上午空出來；如果當年那顆印章沒有被我弄丟，我現在也不會坐在這裡等第十八號。

這些如果一個都沒有成真，我還是坐在這排藍色的椅子上，手裡捏著一本摺角的舊存摺。

輪到我的時候，我站起來把外套拉好走過去，看起來像一個處理得來的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合請假辦事的那天發文，或送給總覺得自己還沒準備好、卻每次都把事情辦完的人。
variations: 如果臨櫃時間再晚一小時，我就不必為了一份文件請半天假。
長大就是明明覺得自己在硬撐，走到櫃檯前還是能把話講清楚。

en.content:
If you'd told me at twenty-two that one day I'd burn half a vacation day sitting in a bank's waiting area to finish one form, I'd have decided that kind of adult sounded pretty dull.

If the teller windows stayed open one more hour, I wouldn't have had to clear an entire morning; if I hadn't lost that seal years ago, I wouldn't be here waiting on number eighteen.

None of those ifs came true, so here I am on this row of blue chairs, holding an old passbook with a folded corner.

When my turn comes, I stand up, straighten my jacket, and walk over looking like someone who has it handled.
en.editorNote: For the day you take leave just to run errands, or for anyone who feels unqualified and gets it done anyway.
variations: One more hour of teller service and I wouldn't be spending half a vacation day on one form.
Growing up is feeling like you're faking it and still explaining yourself clearly at the counter.

items.sourceNote: 北北基計程車起跳價調漲為 85 元的報導；改寫成在後座慢慢放下一個蛋糕盒的特寫

zh-tw.content:
車門關上，我把袋子從肩上卸下來，一格一格放到旁邊的座位。

手放開之後又在袋口上停了兩秒，因為裡面是剛買的蛋糕，我怕它倒。

跳表跳到第二次我才把手收回來，靠上椅背，看著窗外的招牌一塊一塊往後退。

這段路我以前一定會用走的，今天我讓自己坐著，也沒有在腦袋裡算那八十五塊划不划算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合難得對自己好一點的那天發文，或送給總是先算錢才決定要不要休息的人。
variations: 跳表跳到第二次，我才真的把背靠上去。
會心疼錢是一種成熟，偶爾放過自己則是另一種。

en.content:
The door shuts, and I slide the bag off my shoulder and lower it onto the seat beside me, inch by inch.

My hand lets go and then hovers over the opening for two more seconds, because there's a cake in there and I don't want it to tip.

Only when the meter clicks a second time do I pull my hand back, lean into the seat, and watch the signs outside slide past one by one.

A year ago I would have walked this stretch; tonight I let myself sit, and I never once worked out whether the fare was worth it.
en.editorNote: For the rare day you're kind to yourself, or for anyone who prices out rest before allowing it.
variations: The meter clicked twice before I actually let my back touch the seat.
Caring about the cost is one kind of maturity; letting yourself off the hook now and then is another.

items.sourceNote: 動物醫院診療、抽血、超音波等收費項目的整理文章；改寫成診療檯上對一個不在場的人說話的第二人稱獨白

zh-tw.content:
金屬檯面很冰，我先脫下外套鋪上去，才把牠抱上來，這個動作是你教我的。

你說過牠怕鐵，四隻腳一踩到就會發抖，今天牠一樣抖，我一樣鋪外套，只是這次沒有人幫我按住牠的後腿。

醫師講了一串我聽不懂的名詞，抽血兩千八，超音波再加一千五，我說都做，沒有回頭找誰確認。

牠會沒事的，這句話我先講給自己聽，再講給不在這裡的你聽。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人扛起以前兩個人一起做的事那天，也適合送給第一次自己帶毛小孩就醫的朋友。
variations: 有些事你走了以後我才真的學會，學會的那天你不在。
我說都做，講完才發現自己沒有回頭找人確認。

en.content:
The steel table is cold, so I take my jacket off and spread it out before I lift her on — you're the one who taught me that.

You always said she hates metal, that her paws start shaking the second they touch it. She's shaking tonight too, and I laid the jacket down the same way, except this time nobody is here to hold her back legs.

The vet runs through a list of words I don't follow, bloodwork, an ultrasound on top of that, and I say do all of it without turning around to check with anyone.

She's going to be fine. I'm saying that to myself first, and then to you, who isn't here.
en.editorNote: For the day you carry alone what two people used to carry together, or for a friend taking a pet in by themselves for the first time.
variations: Some things I only really learned after you left, and you weren't there on the day I did.
I said do all of it, and only afterward noticed I hadn't looked back at anyone for approval.

items.sourceNote: 遠見整理台灣夜市十五大人氣遊戲、談套圈圈作為童年共同記憶的報導；改寫成同一個攤子前十歲與現在的對照

zh-tw.content:
十歲那年我站在同一個攤子前，五十塊換十個竹圈，全部丟完只套中一個塑膠水杯。

老闆說再買一份就有機會，我回頭找我媽，她說回家吧，我一路唸到坐上她的機車後座還在唸。

今天我又站在同一個位置，錢包裡的錢足夠把整排娃娃搬回家，我還是只買了一份圈。

十個丟完一樣全落空，我笑著跟老闆說謝謝就走了，準頭一點都沒進步，進步的是我肯把一百塊丟進一件明知道沒結果的事，還覺得值得。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合帶小孩逛夜市那天發文，也適合寫給以前總是把每一塊錢都算得很清楚的自己。
variations: 準頭一點都沒進步，進步的是我肯把錢花在明知道沒結果的事情上。
小時候丟不中會賴老闆，現在丟不中，我謝謝他讓我丟。

en.content:
I was ten, standing at this exact stall, where fifty dollars bought ten bamboo rings and all ten of them landed on nothing but a plastic cup.

The owner said one more round and I'd have a shot. I turned to my mom, she said we're going home, and I was still complaining by the time I climbed onto the back of her scooter.

Tonight I'm at the same spot with enough in my wallet to buy every prize on that shelf outright, and I still bought exactly one set of rings.

Ten throws, nothing again, and I thanked the guy and walked off. My aim hasn't improved at all. What improved is that I can spend a hundred on something I know won't work out and still call it money well spent.
en.editorNote: For a night market run with a kid in tow, or for the version of you that used to account for every single dollar.
variations: My aim never improved. What improved is my willingness to pay for something I know won't pan out.
As a kid I blamed the stall owner when I missed. Now I thank him for letting me try.

items.sourceNote: Heho 健康談 35 歲起進入輕熟視力期、微老花與正確矯正的報導；改寫成驗光室裡一句隨口的話改變整件事的意思

zh-tw.content:
驗光師把儀器推到我眼前，要我看清楚鏡片裡那條沒有盡頭的小路。

換到第三片鏡片，他一邊調一邊隨口問我上一副配多久了，我說五年多，他停了半秒說：「難怪你最近會覺得字都在往後縮。」

我這半年一直以為是自己撐不住了，睡不飽、看合約看兩行就要從頭再看一次，原來有一部分只是鏡片舊了。

戴上新的那副走到街上，招牌一次全部對焦；有些疲倦換一副眼鏡就會好，那種其實算便宜的，剩下的才要慢慢處理。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合把「我是不是不行了」誤會了半年的人，也適合提醒身邊的人該去重新驗光了。
variations: 有些累是鏡片舊了，有些累是真的累，先分清楚再說。
他那句話講得很隨便，我卻在回家的路上想了一整趟。

en.content:
The optometrist rolls the machine up to my face and tells me to look down that little road inside the lens, the one that never ends.

Somewhere around the third lens he asks, totally offhand, how long I've had my current pair. I say a bit over five years. He pauses half a second and says that would explain why the letters feel like they're backing away from you.

For six months I'd been assuming I was the problem, not sleeping enough, rereading the same two lines of a contract from the top. Part of it was just old lenses.

I put the new pair on and every sign on the street snaps into focus at once. Some kinds of tired go away when you change your glasses, and that kind is cheap. The rest is what takes time.
en.editorNote: For anyone who spent half a year assuming they were burning out, and for nudging a friend to get their eyes checked.
variations: Some exhaustion is just an old prescription. Some of it is real. Worth telling them apart.
He said it like it was nothing, and I thought about it the whole ride home.

items.sourceNote: TVBS 整理 2026 丙午馬年安太歲的時間、費用與可代辦說明；改寫成結論先行、再往回倒敘替父母代辦的過程

zh-tw.content:
先講結果：那天我從廟口走回機車旁，手裡多了兩張紅色的收據，一張寫我爸，一張寫我媽。

往前倒一小時，我趴在長桌上一格一格填農曆生日，填到我媽那欄才發現年份要打電話回去問。

再往前倒一天，她在電話裡說今年就算了啦反正也沒差，語氣輕得像在講明天會不會下雨。

再往前倒三年，那三年都是她自己來的，天沒亮就出門，把全家人的名字一個一個交出去，從來沒有人問過她要不要有人陪。八百塊而已，我只是不想再讓她一個人走這一趟。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那個每年默默替全家人處理這些小事的媽媽，也適合今年決定自己去辦的人。
variations: 她說今年就算了啦反正也沒差，我聽得出來她根本不這麼想。
八百塊而已，貴的是這麼多年都沒有人問過她。

en.content:
Here's how it ended: I walked back to my scooter from the temple square holding two red receipts, one with my dad's name on it and one with my mom's.

Rewind an hour and I'm hunched over a long table filling in lunar birthdays box by box, and when I reach my mom's row I realize I have to call home to ask for the year.

Rewind a day and she's on the phone telling me to skip it this year, it doesn't really matter either way, in the same tone she'd use for whether it might rain tomorrow.

Rewind three years and she was doing this alone every single time, leaving before sunrise, handing over the whole family's names one by one, and nobody ever asked if she wanted company. It costs eight hundred dollars. I just didn't want her making the trip by herself again.
en.editorNote: For the parent who quietly handles this errand for everyone every year, and for whoever finally decided to take it over.
variations: She told me to skip it this year, and I could hear that she didn't mean it.
It costs eight hundred dollars. The expensive part is that nobody ever asked her.

items.sourceNote: 內政部戶政司印鑑登記問答：印鑑章印面長寬或直徑須一公分以上未逾三公分、不得用原子章；改寫為原創內容

zh-tw.content:
印面規定一公分以上、三公分以內，我在刻印章店的木頭那排前面挑了二十五分鐘。

老師傅問要刻幾個字，我報上三個字，他說三個字最好排，電腦刻九百八，全手工篆刻要兩千九。

我掏九百八的時候忽然算了一筆帳：二十五分鐘、九百八十塊、三個字，換來一枚可以代替我簽字的東西。

十八歲拿到身分證那天我沒什麼感覺，反而是這顆一點五公分的木頭，讓我覺得自己被算進大人那一欄。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給剛去刻人生第一顆正式印章、或正在辦開戶與各種文件的年輕人，也適合當成「成年感什麼時候才真的出現」的貼文開場
variations: 一點五公分的木頭，比十八歲那張身分證更像成年禮。
九百八十塊、二十五分鐘、三個字，成年可以換算得這麼清楚。

en.content:
The rule says the face has to be at least one centimeter across and no more than three. I spent twenty-five minutes at the seal carver's shop just picking a blank.

The old man asked how many characters. Three, I said, and he told me three lays out best: nine hundred and eighty by machine, twenty-nine hundred if he cuts it by hand.

Handing over the nine-eighty, I did the math out loud in my head: twenty-five minutes, nine hundred and eighty dollars, three characters, in exchange for a small object that is allowed to sign for me.

The day my ID card arrived at eighteen I felt nothing. It was this one-and-a-half-centimeter block of wood that finally filed me under adult.
en.editorNote: Good for anyone who just made their first official signature stamp or seal, or for a post about when adulthood actually starts feeling real
variations: One and a half centimeters of wood turned out to be a better coming-of-age ceremony than the ID card.
Nine hundred eighty dollars, twenty-five minutes, three characters — adulthood priced to the last unit.

items.sourceNote: 台灣手工印章店價目：木質牛角六分章電腦刻980元起、半手工2100元起、全手工2900元起；改寫為原創內容

zh-tw.content:
爸爸那顆用了三十年的木頭章缺了一角，蓋出來的姓少了半邊。

我拿去刻印章店重刻，師傅拿放大鏡照了照，說原章一點二公分，半手工兩千一，三天後來拿。

坐在小凳子上等他寫收條，我算起另一組數字：這顆章領過三百多次薪水、蓋過兩份房貸、簽掉一次退休。

三十年、一點二公分、兩千一，我爸大半輩子的重要決定加起來就這麼一小塊木頭；我付了錢，也算是把那把刻刀接了過來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給開始替爸媽跑腿辦事的同輩，或用在父親節、家中長輩退休這類貼文
variations: 三十年只換來一點二公分，可是全家人的大事都蓋在上面。
重刻兩千一，接下那把刻刀是免費的。

en.content:
My dad's wooden name seal, thirty years old, lost a corner, so the surname it prints now comes out missing half a stroke.

I took it to the carving shop. The engraver looked at it through a loupe and said the original is one point two centimeters, twenty-one hundred to recut it half by hand, ready in three days.

While he wrote out the slip I sat on the little stool and totaled up a different set of numbers: this seal has collected three hundred paychecks, stamped two mortgages, and signed off one retirement.

Thirty years, one point two centimeters, twenty-one hundred dollars. Every major decision of my father's life adds up to this small block of wood, and paying for it is how the chisel quietly changed hands.
en.editorNote: For the friend who has started running errands on their parents' behalf, or for a Father's Day or retirement post
variations: Thirty years of my dad's biggest decisions fit inside one point two centimeters.
The recut cost twenty-one hundred. Inheriting the job cost nothing and everything.

items.sourceNote: 臺北市松山區戶政事務所戶政規費一覽表：印鑑登記每次20元、印鑑證明每張20元；改寫為原創內容

zh-tw.content:
印鑑證明一張二十塊，登記那次也是二十塊，我一口氣拿了十二張。

二百六十塊買到的是接下來十二次不必再跑這一趟，平均每一趟二十二塊，比我常喝的那杯拿鐵還便宜。

小時候我以為大人是什麼都會處理的人，長到現在才知道，大人只是算得出來哪一種麻煩比較划算。

那疊紙我壓在包包最底下帶回家，薄薄十二張，重量剛好等於這幾年被磨出來的耐性。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合正在辦繼承、過戶、貸款而不斷跑公家單位的人，或用來調侃自己終於學會一次把事情辦完
variations: 二十二塊買一次不用重跑，這大概是我算過最划算的一筆。
大人的本事，是把每一種麻煩都標上價錢，然後挑便宜的那種。

en.content:
A seal certificate costs twenty dollars a sheet, and registering the seal was another twenty, so I asked for twelve of them at once.

Two hundred sixty dollars buys twelve trips I will never have to make again — about twenty-two dollars a trip, cheaper than the latte I buy without thinking.

As a kid I assumed adults were people who knew how to handle things. Turns out adults are just people who can price which flavor of hassle is the cheaper one.

I carried the stack home at the bottom of my bag. Twelve thin sheets, weighing exactly as much as the patience these last few years cost me.
en.editorNote: For anyone deep in probate, title transfers, or loan paperwork, or for laughing at yourself for finally doing it all in one trip
variations: Twenty-two dollars to never make that trip again is the best deal I have priced this year.
Being an adult means putting a price on every kind of hassle and then picking the cheaper one.

items.sourceNote: 公視新聞：主計總處4月經常性薪資平均49,146元、中位數39,348元；改寫為原創內容

zh-tw.content:
中位數三萬九千三百四十八，我把這個數字抄在便條紙上，貼在冰箱門邊。

我的薪水比它多一點，可是房租一萬二、孝親費六千、保單三千八，扣完之後真正歸我調度的只剩不到一萬。

以前我以為長大是薪水後面多一個零，後來發現長大是把一筆錢切成七份，還要讓每一份都站得住。

那張便條紙貼了四個月，中間被油煙燻黃換過一次，數字沒動過，動的是我終於敢正眼看它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合薪資統計出爐、大家在比對自己站在哪一段時使用，也適合傳給每個月都在切預算的朋友
variations: 同一筆錢切成七份，每一份都要切得平，長大大概就是這門手藝。
數字四個月沒變，變的是我敢盯著它看多久。

en.content:
The median monthly wage came out at 39,348. I copied the number onto a sticky note and put it on the fridge door.

Mine sits a little above it, but rent takes twelve thousand, my parents six, insurance thirty-eight hundred, and what's actually mine to move around is under ten.

I used to think growing up meant another zero on the paycheck. It turns out growing up means cutting one sum into seven pieces and making every piece hold.

That sticky note stayed up four months and got replaced once after the kitchen air yellowed it. The number never moved. What moved was my willingness to look straight at it.
en.editorNote: Use it when wage statistics drop and everyone is checking where they land, or send it to the friend who rebuilds their budget every month
variations: Growing up is a knife skill: one sum, seven pieces, every piece even enough to hold.
The number held still for four months. My ability to look at it is what changed.

items.sourceNote: 臺灣大學總務處出納組學雜費繳費須知（繳費期間、繳費管道）；作為註冊費繳費情境的背景參考，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
「你那個存錢筒先別動。」我媽在飯桌上講完這句，就把註冊費的單子折成四折塞進包包。

那年我十七歲，只覺得她今天話很少，繼續低頭扒飯。

換成我自己在手機上算幾號要匯錢之後，才聽懂那句話是把最重的那一段先搬走。

存錢筒跟著搬過三次家還在，投幣口朝上，我一次也沒去動它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學季、學費繳納期間分享，也適合傳給那個現在才看懂家裡當年怎麼撐過來的朋友
variations: 短版：她只說存錢筒先別動，然後把那張單子折成四折。
延伸版：那個存錢筒現在放在我書桌角落，投幣口還是朝上，我把它當成一句沒有回完的話。

en.content:
"Leave your coin bank alone for now." My mom said that at dinner, then folded the tuition bill into quarters and slid it into her purse.

I was seventeen. All I noticed was that she was quiet that night, so I went back to my rice.

Years later I was the one counting days on my phone until a transfer was due, and that sentence finally made sense: she had picked up the heaviest part before anyone could offer to help carry it.

The coin bank has survived three moves. The slot still faces up, and I have never once dug into it.
en.editorNote: Good for the start of a school term or tuition season, and for the friend who only recently understood how their family got through those years
variations: Short: She just said to leave the coin bank alone, then folded the bill into quarters.
Extended: That coin bank sits on the corner of my desk now, slot facing up, like a sentence I never finished answering.

items.sourceNote: 維基百科「撲滿」條目：名稱意為滿則撲之、傳統只有投幣口需打破取錢、家長給孩子培養儲蓄習慣；作為題材背景，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
「滿了再說。」阿嬤把撲滿推回我這邊的時候，只講了這三個字。

我那時想的是滿了要買哪一台遙控車，她想的大概是那個冬天還有多長。

後來我在自己租的地方擺了一個差不多的，米色塑膠，投幣口有點卡。

它到今天都沒滿過，我卻常常在心裡回她一個好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊童年儲蓄記憶、或想念長輩的時候使用，也適合搭配老照片發文
variations: 短版：滿了再說——那三個字我拿來用了二十年。
延伸版：米色那個到今天都沒滿，可是每次投錢我都會在心裡回她一個好。

en.content:
"We'll talk when it's full." That was all my grandmother said as she pushed the piggy bank back across the table to me.

I was thinking about which remote-control car I would buy when it filled up. She was probably thinking about how long that winter still had to run.

Years later I put a similar one in my own rented place, beige plastic, with a slot that sticks a little.

It has never filled up. I still answer her out loud sometimes, just an okay, to nobody.
en.editorNote: Use it when talking about childhood saving habits or missing a grandparent, and it pairs well with an old family photo
variations: Short: We'll talk when it's full — three words I have been living on for twenty years.
Extended: The beige one has never filled up, but every coin I drop in gets an okay from me under my breath.

items.sourceNote: 經濟日報：yes123調查39歲以下青年平均存款14.9萬、七成三背債；作為職場世代處境背景，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
「你先吃，我等一下。」前輩在微波爐前面說過這句，那天他明明站在我前面。

當時我以為他只是不餓。

三年後換我對新來的同事講同樣五個字，才知道那是把二十分鐘的午休讓出去一半。

辦公室的微波爐換過一台了，這句話還是在同一個位置被講出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在辦公室午休、帶新人的時候分享，也適合傳給那個總是讓別人先的同事
variations: 短版：你先吃，我等一下——同一台微波爐前面，我從聽的人變成講的人。
延伸版：微波爐換過一台，那五個字沒換過，只是講的人變成我。

en.content:
"You go ahead, I'll wait." A senior coworker said that in front of the office microwave, even though he had gotten there before me.

At the time I assumed he just wasn't hungry.

Three years later I said the same five words to the new hire, and understood that it meant handing over half of a twenty-minute lunch break.

The office has replaced that microwave since. The sentence still gets said in exactly the same spot.
en.editorNote: Good for office lunch breaks or when you're onboarding someone new, and for the coworker who always lets everyone else go first
variations: Short: You go ahead, I'll wait — same microwave, except now I'm the one saying it.
Extended: The microwave got replaced. The five words didn't. Only the person saying them changed.

items.sourceNote: 聯合新聞網：台壽與政大調查國人平均42.73歲才有能力存退休金、六成未退族每月存不到1萬；作為金錢焦慮背景，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
「這個月先這樣。」我爸每次講完就把存摺闔起來，語氣跟報明天天氣一樣平。

小時候我聽不出這五個字有什麼特別，只記得存摺封面是深藍色，邊角磨到起毛。

現在我在月底也會講同樣五個字，講給沒有人聽。

深藍色那本早就換成手機裡的一行數字，句子倒是原封不動被我接了過來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合月底對帳、或跟朋友聊家裡的金錢氣氛時使用，也適合傳給正在學著接住家計的人
variations: 短版：這個月先這樣——我爸的語氣像在報天氣，我現在也學會了。
延伸版：深藍色的存摺換成手機裡一行數字，那五個字連語調都被我接了過來。

en.content:
"This month we'll manage." My dad would say it and close the passbook, in the same flat tone people use for tomorrow's forecast.

As a kid I heard nothing special in those four words. I just remember the passbook cover was dark blue, worn fuzzy at the corners.

Now I say the same thing at the end of the month, out loud, to an empty room.

The dark blue book turned into one line of digits on a phone. The sentence came through intact, tone and all.
en.editorNote: Use it when you're reconciling accounts at month's end or talking with friends about the money atmosphere at home, and for anyone learning to carry the household
variations: Short: This month we'll manage — my dad reported it like weather, and now so do I.
Extended: The dark blue passbook became a line of digits on a phone. The sentence survived the migration, tone included.

items.sourceNote: 慶泰小學堂：竹蒸籠使用前需泡水十二小時以上、中途至少換三次水去竹鹼，晾乾後再用才不易變形；作為新手備器情境的背景參考，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
搬進來第三天，我把新買的蒸籠壓進水槽，上面壓兩個空玻璃罐，它還是翹起一角。

說明上寫泡滿十二小時、中間換三次水，我把鬧鐘設在凌晨兩點、清晨六點、上午十點。

第二次換水那趟，我蹲在水槽邊，指腹沿著竹片的縫來回摸了八遍，才把翹起來那角重新壓進水裡。

天亮我把它撈出來立在流理臺上晾，拍了一張照片，沒有傳給任何人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛搬進第一個自己的住處、或開始買像樣廚具的時候分享，也適合搭配新器具的開箱照
variations: 短版：新蒸籠要泡滿十二小時，我為它設了三個鬧鐘，第二個在凌晨兩點。
延伸版：那張照片還在相簿裡，構圖很正，光線也對，就是一直沒有找到可以傳的對象。

en.content:
Third day in the new apartment, I pushed the new bamboo steamer down into the sink, weighted it with two empty jars, and one edge still tipped up.

The instructions said soak it a full twelve hours and change the water three times, so I set alarms for two in the morning, six, and ten.

On the second change I crouched by the sink and ran my fingertip along the seams between the slats eight times before that edge finally stayed under.

At daylight I lifted it out and stood it on the counter to dry, took one photo of it, and sent it to nobody.
en.editorNote: Good for the week you move into your first place of your own, or the first time you buy real cookware, and it pairs well with an unboxing shot
variations: Short: A new bamboo steamer needs twelve hours underwater. I set three alarms for it. The second one went off at two in the morning.
Extended: The photo is still in my camera roll, well framed, decently lit, and I never did find anyone to send it to.

items.sourceNote: 聯合新聞網：過年蒸年糕的傳統禁忌，旁人不可詢問「蒸多久」「熟了沒」，長輩多會禁止小孩靠近或出聲；作為年節場景的背景參考，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
阿嬤蒸甜粿那天，用手背把我往後推了半步，指了指離蒸籠一公尺遠的矮凳。

我坐上去，看白煙從蒸籠邊緣一圈一圈推出來，數到第十七圈就數亂了。

那三個小時她一句話都沒說，我把「好了沒」三個字吞回去，只換了四次坐姿。

掀蓋那一刻她讓我先看，我伸手戳了一下，指腹陷進去半個指節，她才把爐火關小。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合過年前後聊家裡的年節規矩時分享，也適合傳給那個現在換自己站在爐前的人
variations: 短版：她把我推到一公尺外的矮凳上，那三個小時我只換了四次坐姿。
延伸版：現在輪到我蒸，我也會先把靠過來的人推開半步，然後把那張矮凳往後拉。

en.content:
The day my grandmother steamed the new year cake, she pushed me back half a step with the back of her hand and pointed at a low stool a meter from the steamer.

I sat down and watched white steam roll out from the rim of the steamer in rings, and lost count somewhere around the seventeenth.

For three hours she did not say a word, and I swallowed the question about whether it was done, shifting how I sat exactly four times.

When she lifted the lid she let me look first; I poked it once, my fingertip sank in half a knuckle, and only then did she turn the flame down.
en.editorNote: Good around the Lunar New Year when families talk about their kitchen rules, and for anyone who now stands at the stove themselves
variations: Short: She moved me to a stool a meter away. In three hours I shifted position exactly four times.
Extended: It is my turn to steam it now, and I still push people back half a step before pulling that stool away from the heat.

items.sourceNote: 遠見雜誌：全台一人宅十年成長57%、單身未婚戶長大幅增加，一人份餐飲與小份量食品成為常態；作為獨居飲食場景的背景參考，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
星期天早上我把蒸籠架上鍋，鋪一張烘焙紙，擺兩顆冷凍的包子，中間留一個指頭的寬度。

水滾後轉中火十四分鐘，我把手機倒扣在流理臺上，看白氣從竹縫一直冒。

時間到掀蓋，我夾一顆進碗裡，另一顆用夾子推到蒸籠正中間，蓋子重新蓋回去。

那顆在裡面又待了四十分鐘，等我把碗洗好、桌子擦過兩遍，才被夾出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人住、週末自己張羅早餐的時候分享，也適合傳給那個總是煮兩人份的朋友
variations: 短版：我蒸了兩顆，吃完一顆，另一顆推到正中間，蓋子蓋回去。
延伸版：第二顆放涼的速度我現在很清楚，四十分鐘，跟我把碗洗好、桌子擦兩遍的時間剛好一樣。

en.content:
Sunday morning I set the bamboo steamer on the pot, laid down a sheet of parchment, and placed two frozen buns a finger's width apart.

Once the water boiled I turned it to medium for fourteen minutes, set my phone face down on the counter, and watched steam push out through the woven gaps.

When the timer went off I lifted the lid, moved one bun into a bowl, nudged the other to the exact center with the tongs, and put the lid back on.

That one sat in there another forty minutes, until I had washed the bowl and wiped the table twice, before it came out.
en.editorNote: Good for anyone living alone who cooks their own weekend breakfast, and for the friend who still makes portions for two
variations: Short: I steamed two, ate one, nudged the other to the center, and put the lid back on.
Extended: I know exactly how long the second one takes to go cold now. Forty minutes, the same as washing one bowl and wiping the table twice.

items.sourceNote: 食力foodNEXT：台灣外食比例近七成、家戶自炊比例下降的飲食文化轉變；作為週末備餐情境的背景參考，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
每個星期天晚上我把五個便當盒排開，蓋子一律翻過來墊在盒底下。

裝飯的時候用湯匙背壓三下，壓到看不見縫隙，五盒的重量差不多一樣。

最左邊那盒我會多放一塊肉，那盒是留給星期五的，星期五我通常九點多才進門。

五個蓋子扣上去的聲音一樣，我一個一個推進冰箱，門合起來會頂到最外面那盒。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合週末備餐、或聊自己怎麼把一週撐過去的時候分享，也適合傳給同樣在星期天晚上煮飯的人
variations: 短版：五個便當盒，湯匙背壓三下，只有最左邊那盒多一塊肉。
延伸版：多的那塊肉是星期五的，我從來沒算過它多重，只知道那天需要多一點。

en.content:
